findings.runtimeMechanismMd: Operation invocation uses named query parameters for GET and named `Parameters.parameter` parts for POST. R4 clients, generated SDKs, and conformance tests often treat these names as the method signature. In R6, the formal names change and `reverse` is removed, so old request builders can produce requests that are syntactically well-formed HTTP/FHIR but semantically invalid for the R6 OperationDefinition. Servers that are lenient may accept some old names, but the base R6 contract only makes old `system` and `version` optional server aliases and leaves the rest out.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate clients from the R6 OperationDefinition and update request mappings explicitly: `code` to `sourceCode`, `system` to `sourceSystem`, `version` to `sourceVersion`, `coding` to `sourceCoding`, `codeableConcept` to `sourceCodeableConcept`, `source` to `sourceScope`, `target` to `targetScope`, `targetsystem` to `targetSystem`, and `dependency.element/concept` to `dependency.attribute/value`. Replace `reverse=true` requests by placing the known concept in `targetCode`, `targetCoding`, or `targetCodeableConcept` and supplying source/target scopes or systems as appropriate. R6 servers that want to ease migration should document and test any legacy aliases they accept, because only `system` and `version` are mentioned by the base text.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The inferred R6 goal is to make translation direction explicit and align the operation with R6 ConceptMap mappings where a known concept may be on either the source or target side. That is a reasonable goal. A less-breaking base design appears available: preserve R4 names as deprecated formal aliases while adding the R6 names, and define conflict rules when old and new names are mixed. This would add duplicate representations and implementation burden, but it would preserve common R4 requests and is suggested by the R6 decision to allow legacy `system` and `version` as optional server behavior. Because the alias approach could have been comprehensive and low-to-moderate cost, the current break is probably avoidable enough to merit review.

findings.title: R6 changes the match output shape from equivalence/source/product concept to relationship, properties, dependencies, and originMap

oldValue.name: match.equivalence
oldValue.documentation: uses ConceptMapEquivalence

newValue.name: match.relationship
newValue.documentation: uses ConceptMapRelationship

changedFields.note: R6 renames the output part and changes the relationship vocabulary referenced by the operation documentation.

changedFields.oldValue: True only if at least one returned match has an equivalence which is not unmatched or disjoint.
changedFields.newValue: True only if at least one returned match has a relationship other than 'not-related-to'.
changedFields.note: The output success rule changes with the equivalence-to-relationship terminology.
The product part is renamed, widened, and its child parts become required when a product is present.
R6 adds property and dependsOn outputs and renames the concept-map source reference to `originMap`.

parameterDeltas.name: match.equivalence/match.relationship

oldValue.name: equivalence
oldValue.documentation: A code indicating the equivalence of the translation, using values from ConceptMapEquivalence.

newValue.name: relationship
newValue.documentation: A code indicating the relationship of the translation, using values from ConceptMapRelationship.

parameterDeltas.impactMd: R4 output parsers that look for `match.equivalence` will miss the relationship in an R6 response. Enum switches also need to move from old equivalence codes such as `unmatched`/`disjoint` to relationship codes such as `not-related-to`.

parameterDeltas.name: match.product
parameterDeltas.impactMd: R6 product data is not just a rename: a product has required attribute/value children, and the value can be a generic Element rather than only a Coding.

parameterDeltas.name: match.property
parameterDeltas.impactMd: R6 servers may return mapping priority, provenance, presentation hints, experimental flags, or other properties in a standard output part that has no R4 output equivalent.

parameterDeltas.name: match.dependsOn
parameterDeltas.impactMd: R6 can return additional attribute conditions that were not part of the R4 match output.

parameterDeltas.name: match.source/match.originMap
parameterDeltas.impactMd: R4 clients that use `match.source` to identify the originating concept map need to read the formal R6 `match.originMap` part. The R6 narrative examples currently show `originalMap`, so implementers should follow the OperationDefinition and watch for errata.

findings.matchRationaleMd: The operations are the same canonical `ConceptMap/$translate` operation. The output differences are changes to the response `Parameters` contract for the same endpoint, not separate resources or unrelated ConceptMap StructureDefinition findings.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Strict R4-generated clients and validators commonly model `match.equivalence`, `match.concept`, optional `match.product.element/concept`, and `match.source`. R6 responses use different names and may include richer property, dependsOn, and Element-valued product data, so R4 parsers can fail or silently drop key semantics. Downgrading R6 results to the R4 operation shape is lossy for relationship details that do not map cleanly to R4 equivalence, arbitrary Element values, properties, and dependsOn outputs.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `ConceptMap-translate` is standards-status `trial-use` and FMM 3. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A mapping service client generated from the R4 OperationDefinition receives an R6 response with `match.relationship=equivalent`, `match.product.attribute/value`, and `match.originMap`. Its decoder looks for `match.equivalence`, `match.product.concept`, and `match.source`, so it treats the match as missing equivalence/source details or rejects the response as containing unknown parts.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: R6 could have kept deprecated output aliases such as `match.equivalence`, `match.source`, and `match.product.element/concept` alongside the new `relationship`, `originMap`, and attribute/value shape for cases where the mapping is unambiguous.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: That would preserve some R4 clients, but it would create duplicate representations and incomplete mappings. R6 properties, dependsOn values, and generic Element-valued products cannot always be represented as R4 Coding-based product concepts, and old equivalence codes do not fully match the R6 relationship code system.

freshReview.rationaleMd: Less-breaking aliases could cover simple cases but would be incomplete and risk inconsistent duplicate outputs. The formal/narrative `originMap` versus `originalMap` inconsistency should be corrected, but it does not make the overall output redesign unjustified.

evidence.detail: R4 match output parts are `equivalence`, `concept`, `product.element`, `product.concept`, and `source`.
evidence.quote: match.equivalence 0..1 code; match.concept 0..1 Coding; match.product 0..*; match.product.element 0..1 uri; match.product.concept 0..1 Coding; match.source 0..1 uri

evidence.detail: R6 match output parts are `relationship`, `concept`, `property.uri/value`, `product.attribute/value`, `dependsOn.attribute/value`, and `originMap`.
evidence.quote: match.relationship 0..1 code; match.concept 0..1 Coding; match.property 0..*; match.property.uri 1..1 uri; match.property.value 1..1 Element; match.product.attribute 1..1 uri; match.product.value 1..1 Element; match.dependsOn.attribute 1..1 uri; match.dependsOn.value 1..1 Element; match.originMap 0..1 uri

evidence.detail: The R4 operation page renders the old result rule and old match output parts.
evidence.quote: result ... equivalence which is not unmatched or disjoint ... match.equivalence ... ConceptMapEquivalence ... match.product.element ... match.product.concept ... match.source

evidence.detail: The R6 operation page renders the new result rule and new match output parts.
evidence.quote: result ... relationship other than 'not-related-to' ... match.relationship ... ConceptMapRelationship ... match.property.uri ... match.product.attribute ... match.dependsOn.attribute ... match.originMap

evidence.detail: The R6 examples use `originalMap`, while the formal R6 OperationDefinition and parameter table use `originMap`.
evidence.quote: "name": "originalMap", "valueString": "http://hl7.org/fhir/ConceptMap/102"

evidence.detail: R6 ConceptMap target elements include relationship, property, dependsOn, and product structures that align with the R6 operation output; this report does not assess the resource StructureDefinition change itself.
evidence.quote: ConceptMap.group.element.target.relationship 1..1 code; target.property; target.dependsOn.attribute/value; target.product

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The operation response is a `Parameters` resource, and the names of nested output parts are the stable API surface for generated clients and validators. R6 changes the nested names and value shapes, so R4 output wrappers can fail at decode time, produce false conformance failures, or silently lose relationship/provenance details. Robust clients that preserve unknown parameters will fare better but still need new logic to interpret `relationship`, `property`, `dependsOn`, and Element-valued products.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update response parsers and tests to read `match.relationship` and the ConceptMapRelationship code system, not `match.equivalence`. Treat `not-related-to` as the R6 explicit no-translation relationship for the result rule. Rename `match.source` handling to the formal `match.originMap`, but monitor the R6 examples that currently say `originalMap`. Replace product parsing with `match.product.attribute` plus `match.product.value`, and preserve optional `match.property` and `match.dependsOn` repeats even if the application does not immediately use them. R4 bridge layers should document which R6 relationship/property/dependency/product values are dropped or approximated.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The inferred R6 goal is to expose the richer R6 ConceptMap mapping model directly in `$translate` results: relationships rather than equivalences, arbitrary mapping properties, mapping dependencies, and attribute/value products. That goal is reasonable and difficult to meet fully through the R4 output shape. A less-breaking design could have added deprecated aliases for simple values, but aliases would be partial and could create inconsistent duplicate representations. For this output finding, the compatibility cost appears proportionate, although the `originMap`/`originalMap` example inconsistency should be corrected.

findings.title: R6 terminology server example advertises ConceptMap-translate with operation name expand

changedFields.note: The local R6 terminology-server example references the ConceptMap translate OperationDefinition but gives the operation name as `expand`. The base CapabilityStatement still has a system-level `translate` operation with the same lowercase definition form used in R4.

findings.matchRationaleMd: This is not a change to the OperationDefinition identity. It is an operation-specific CapabilityStatement advertisement issue discovered while checking local core CapabilityStatement files for the same `ConceptMap-translate` canonical operation.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The likely error is confined to a local R6 example/instance CapabilityStatement, so it is less likely to break deployed clients than the OperationDefinition parameter changes. However, CapabilityStatements drive generated clients, conformance tests, and operation discovery. A client that trusts this example could generate or test a ConceptMap `$expand` advertisement while missing `$translate`, even though the definition points to ConceptMap-translate.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `ConceptMap-translate` is standards-status `trial-use` and FMM 3. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A conformance-test generator loads the R6 terminology server example and sees a ConceptMap resource operation named `expand` whose definition is `ConceptMap-translate`. It generates a check for `[base]/ConceptMap/[id]/$expand` or fails to detect advertised `$translate` support.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: Use `name: "translate"` for the operation entry that points to `http://hl7.org/fhir/OperationDefinition/ConceptMap-translate`, and optionally advertise it at the same system or resource level intended by the terminology server example.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: There is no meaningful design tradeoff: the operation name should match the OperationDefinition code. If the example intended to advertise ValueSet `$expand`, it should point to the ValueSet expand OperationDefinition instead.

freshReview.rationaleMd: This appears to be a low-cost metadata correction with a concrete operation-discovery failure mode. Because the R6 goal can be met by making the name and definition consistent, this deserves renewed standards/editorial attention.

evidence.detail: The R4 terminology server CapabilityStatement advertises `translate` with definition `OperationDefinition/ConceptMap-translate` and SHALL expectation.
evidence.quote: {"name":"translate","definition":"OperationDefinition/ConceptMap-translate"}

evidence.detail: The R6 example terminology server CapabilityStatement advertises a ConceptMap resource operation named `expand` but points to the ConceptMap translate OperationDefinition.
evidence.quote: {"name":"expand","definition":"http://hl7.org/fhir/OperationDefinition/ConceptMap-translate"}

evidence.detail: The R4 base CapabilityStatement has a system-level operation named `translate` pointing to the lowercase ConceptMap translate definition URL.
evidence.quote: {"name":"translate","definition":"http://hl7.org/fhir/OperationDefinition/conceptmap-translate"}

evidence.detail: The R6 base CapabilityStatement retains the same system-level `translate` advertisement form as R4.
evidence.quote: {"name":"translate","definition":"http://hl7.org/fhir/OperationDefinition/conceptmap-translate"}

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: FHIR operation discovery uses `CapabilityStatement.rest.operation.name` or `rest.resource.operation.name` as the operation code to advertise. If the name says `expand` while the definition points to `ConceptMap-translate`, a metadata-driven client or test harness can derive the wrong operation endpoint or report inconsistent server capabilities. The risk is limited by the fact that the base CapabilityStatement still advertises `translate` and the problematic R6 artifact is an example/instance CapabilityStatement.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not infer ConceptMap `$translate` support from the R6 example entry named `expand` without checking the OperationDefinition code. Implementers publishing R6 CapabilityStatements should advertise `name: "translate"` for `ConceptMap-translate`. Test suites should flag name/definition mismatches and prefer the OperationDefinition code when reconciling inconsistent example metadata.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The inferred intended goal is to advertise terminology server support for ConceptMap `$translate`. The R6 example can meet that goal without any compatibility break by using operation name `translate`. If the row intended to advertise `$expand`, the definition should be ValueSet-expand instead. Because the less-breaking and more correct design is simply to make name and definition consistent, the current example is not clearly justified.

findings.matchRationaleMd: The deterministic fanout classifies this shard as `r4-only` with match method `unmatched`: the R4 package has `OperationDefinition-Encounter-everything.json`, while the R6 package and index have no Encounter-scoped OperationDefinition with the same canonical URL, id, resource/code pair, or case-insensitive file name. Other R6 `$everything` OperationDefinitions are scoped to Group and MedicinalProductDefinition, not Encounter. The R6 rendered pages are therefore treated as conflicting narrative evidence, not as a computable package match.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 clients can continue to make the same HTTP call only if an R6 server independently implements it. A server, generated SDK, validator, or test suite generated from the R6 core package or base CapabilityStatement will not discover the Encounter `$everything` operation and may omit the route or reject the canonical OperationDefinition reference. The R6 narrative pages reduce the chance that the intended behavior was truly removed, but increase the interoperability risk because page-driven and package-driven implementations will disagree.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `Encounter-everything` is standards-status `trial-use` and FMM 2. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A SMART-on-FHIR client or test harness generated from the R6 package checks a server's CapabilityStatement and generated operation registry before calling `GET /Encounter/123/$everything`; because the R6 package and base CapabilityStatement omit the operation, the client treats the operation as unsupported even though the R6 HTML page says it exists.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: If R6 intended to retain Encounter `$everything`, keep `OperationDefinition-Encounter-everything` in the core package and package index under the existing canonical URL, add `affectsState: false`, keep the R4-compatible route and parameters, and keep the base CapabilityStatement and operations list aligned with the narrative. If R6 intended to retire it, keep a deprecated or informative legacy OperationDefinition for one release and make the rendered pages explicit about deprecation and migration.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Keeping the artifact has low apparent cost because the R6 pages already publish the same operation and R6 still carries other `$everything` OperationDefinitions. The tradeoff is continuing to expose a broad data-retrieval operation in computable conformance surfaces, but that is already implied by the R6 narrative.

freshReview.rationaleMd: This deserves fresh standards/design attention because the R6 sources disagree on whether a normative-looking operation exists. The break is avoidable by aligning the computable package, CapabilityStatement, and operations list with the already-published R6 pages, or by documenting a deliberate retirement path.

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The concrete mechanism is operation discovery and generated API loss. R4-aware clients, servers, validators, and conformance tests can discover and model `Encounter/[id]/$everything` from the R4 OperationDefinition and base CapabilityStatement. R6 package-driven tooling cannot discover a computable operation, so generated clients may not expose a method, generated servers may not register a route, validators may not validate request/response `Parameters` or direct Bundle output, and conformance tests may treat the canonical operation as absent. The R6 HTML pages still documenting the operation means human implementers may do the opposite, creating cross-implementation inconsistency.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not rely on the R6 core package alone to decide whether an R6 server supports Encounter `$everything`; check the server's CapabilityStatement, implementation guide, or explicit OperationDefinition publication. Servers that want R4 compatibility should publish the legacy canonical OperationDefinition or a clearly equivalent local artifact, advertise it, and keep `_since`, `_type`, `_count`, and direct searchset Bundle behavior compatible. Test suites should flag the R6 package/page inconsistency separately from a server's voluntary support for the operation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The inferred R6 goal is unclear. If the goal was to retire Encounter `$everything`, the R6 operation pages should not continue to publish it as a formal/normative-looking operation without a migration note. If the goal was only publication cleanup or package curation, the same goal could have been accomplished with a less-breaking design by retaining the computable OperationDefinition and aligning CapabilityStatement/operationslist entries with the already-published narrative. Because that alternative is low-cost and preserves the R4 canonical surface, the current package omission appears avoidable.

findings.title: R6 narrative removes the R4 US Realm DAF/meaningful-use returned-data SHALL

changedFields.oldValue: In the US Realm, at a minimum, the resources returned SHALL include all the data covered by the meaningful use common data elements, with DAF cited for further guidance.
changedFields.newValue: Implementation guides may make additional rules about how much information is returned.
changedFields.note: R6 removes the base operation narrative's US-specific minimum returned-data `SHALL` rather than replacing it with an R6 core obligation.

findings.matchRationaleMd: This finding compares the R4 and R6 rendered Encounter `$everything` narrative pages, both of which publish the same operation route and parameter shape. The change is operation-specific conformance text about how complete the returned records must be, not a resource/datatype StructureDefinition change.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a request/response schema break: `_since`, `_type`, `_count`, and the searchset Bundle output remain the same in the rendered pages. The practical break is semantic and conformance-oriented. R4 US Realm tests or client expectations that used the base operation page's DAF/meaningful-use `SHALL` as a minimum completeness rule no longer have that base R6 hook and must rely on an implementation guide or server contract.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `Encounter-everything` is standards-status `trial-use` and FMM 2. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A US conformance test written for an R4 server checks that `Encounter/123/$everything` includes all meaningful-use common data elements because the R4 operation page said the US Realm SHALL include them; the same test cannot cite the R6 base operation page because the R6 text delegates such rules to implementation guides.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: R6 could have kept a non-normative compatibility note saying that US Realm IGs such as US Core may impose minimum returned-data rules, or it could have retained a clearly deprecated DAF/meaningful-use note while removing the base `SHALL`.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Keeping a US-specific SHALL in international core would be a poor long-term base design, especially when DAF/meaningful-use guidance is obsolete and IG-specific obligations are more appropriate. A compatibility note would reduce surprise but would not preserve the original enforceable conformance rule.

freshReview.rationaleMd: There is a real conformance migration burden for R4 US workflows that treated the sentence as a base requirement, but the R6 goal of moving jurisdiction-specific completeness rules out of international core and into implementation guides is reasonable. The less-breaking option is only partial because preserving the exact R4 SHALL would carry material governance and scope tradeoffs.

evidence.detail: R4 narrative includes a US Realm minimum returned-data SHALL tied to meaningful-use common data elements and DAF.
evidence.quote: In the US Realm, at a mimimum, the resources returned SHALL include all the data covered by the meaningful use common data elements

evidence.detail: R6 narrative replaces the US Realm SHALL with a general implementation-guide delegation and a separate ambiguity note.
evidence.quote: Implementation guides may make additional rules about how much information that is returned.

evidence.detail: The rendered R6 input and output parameter table remains the same, so this finding is about narrative returned-resource semantics rather than parameter shape.
evidence.quote: _since 0..1 instant; _type 0..* code; _count 0..1 integer; return 1..1 Bundle

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The mechanism is not a validator rejecting a differently shaped request. It is loss of a base conformance expectation about response completeness.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move US-specific completeness expectations to the applicable R6 implementation guide, certification criterion, or server contract. Clients should treat R6 base Encounter `$everything` as defining the route and general inclusion principles, not a US Realm minimum data set. Servers that want R4 compatibility can document and test the old returned-data minimum as an IG/profile obligation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: international core should not hard-code a US Realm DAF/meaningful-use returned-data SHALL, especially as current US requirements live in IGs. A less-breaking design could have retained a compatibility note or pointed to current US Realm IGs, but preserving the exact R4 SHALL in base R6 would have carried material scope and maintenance tradeoffs.

findings.title: List $find is removed from R6 with no direct operation replacement

changedFields.note: No R6 OperationDefinition with this canonical URL, id, or same List/find operation code was found in the R6 core package.

changedFields.oldValue: find
changedFields.note: The executable `$find` route segment for List disappears from the R6 core operation set.
R4 permitted type-level invocation only. R6 has no base List `$find` route.

The R4 JSON artifact does not carry a computable affectsState value, but the R4 operation page states the operation is idempotent. Removal means there is no R6 statefulness declaration for this operation.

changedFields.oldValue: patient 1..1 id; name 1..1 code; no nested parts, bindings, profiles, or target profiles.
changedFields.note: Both required input parameters are removed with the operation. R6 has no base Parameters schema for locating a functional List by patient id and functional-list code.

changedFields.oldValue: No formal out parameters; narrative success body is the located List resource with HTTP 200 OK, and not found is HTTP 404 optionally with OperationOutcome.
changedFields.note: The R4 operation-specific response behavior is removed. This is not a Parameters output-shape change so much as the disappearance of the route that returned a List resource directly.

changedFields.oldValue: The R4 narrative describes finding an identified list for a patient and functional-list name, points to Current Resource Lists, and says applications may define additional lists. It also notes servers may support searching by functional list without supporting this direct operation.
changedFields.note: R6 has no List-find operation narrative page. The R4 note about search as an alternative is important mitigation context, not a direct operation replacement.
The R4 base CapabilityStatement advertises the find operation. The R6 base CapabilityStatement omits it.

changedFields.oldValue: [base]/List/$find
changedFields.note: The rendered R4 operations list includes List `$find`; the R6 operations list has no List `$find` row.

parameterDeltas.name: patient

oldValue.documentation: The id of a patient resource located on the server on which this operation is executed

parameterDeltas.impactMd: R4 requests had to identify the patient for whom the functional List was being found. In R6 there is no base List `$find` parameter to carry this patient id, so generated clients and validators lose the required request member.

parameterDeltas.name: name

oldValue.documentation: The code for the functional list that is being found

parameterDeltas.impactMd: R4 requests had to provide the functional-list code, such as a current-allergies-style list name. R6 has no same operation parameter, so a request cannot be mechanically converted to an R6 List `$find` call.

findings.matchRationaleMd: The operation-fanout manifest classifies this shard as `r4-only` and `unmatched`. The R4 operation has canonical URL `http://hl7.org/fhir/OperationDefinition/List-find`, resource `List`, and code `find`; the R6 package contains no `OperationDefinition-List-find.json` and no `OperationDefinition-*find*.json` candidate. The R6 `_list` search parameter is useful migration context but is not a same-canonical OperationDefinition replacement because it searches resources by list membership rather than exposing `[base]/List/$find` to return the List resource itself.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct operation/API break for implementations that used the R4 route or generated code from the R4 OperationDefinition: a client invoking `[base]/List/$find?patient=example&name=$current-allergies` against a strict R6 server should not assume the operation exists, and generated R6 client/server stubs and operation validators will not include the R4 request contract. Conformance tests that expected the R4 base CapabilityStatement operation advertisement also need revision. The prevalence is likely rare because the operation was draft, FMM 1, trial-use, type-level only, and the R4 narrative explicitly says servers may support searching by functional list without supporting this direct operation.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `List-find` is standards-status `trial-use` and FMM 1. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: An EHR client generated an R4 SDK method for `List/$find` and used `GET /ehr/fhir/List/$find?patient=example&name=$current-allergies` to retrieve a patient's current allergy List resource. After regenerating from R6, the SDK method and server route are absent, and a conformance test looking for `CapabilityStatement.rest.operation[find]` fails.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: R6 could have retained `OperationDefinition/List-find` with the same canonical URL, `draft` or `retired` status, and the same two required inputs, while omitting it from the base CapabilityStatement and adding narrative that `_list` search is the preferred functional-list mechanism.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: This only partially meets the likely R6 goal. Keeping the artifact in core would continue to surface a redundant low-maturity route and could cause generators or conformance tools to keep presenting it as part of the base operation catalog. If the goal was to simplify the base standard around `_list` search and stop encouraging direct functional-List lookup, hard removal is cleaner even though it is more disruptive for early adopters.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The change is a real runtime/API and conformance break, but the affected operation was low maturity, optional in practice, and overlapped with a search mechanism that remains available for many functional-list retrieval workflows. A less-breaking retired-artifact design was plausible for tooling continuity, but it has material tradeoffs because it would keep a deprecated route in the core operation catalog. Given the FMM 1 trial-use status, explicit R4 caveat, and lack of evidence of broad production reliance, the removal looks proportionate rather than a fresh-review `Revisit` case.

evidence.detail: R4 defines OperationDefinition id List-find, canonical URL http://hl7.org/fhir/OperationDefinition/List-find, code find, resource List, system=false, type=true, instance=false, status draft, standards-status trial-use, FMM 1, and required input parameters patient and name.
evidence.quote: "parameter":[{"name":"patient","use":"in","min":1,"max":"1","type":"id"},{"name":"name","use":"in","min":1,"max":"1","type":"code"}]

evidence.detail: The R4 operation page renders FMM/status, purpose, canonical URL, invocation URL, idempotence, input parameter table, and the note that search may be supported instead of the direct operation.
evidence.quote: Maturity Level: 1; Trial Use; URL: [base]/List/$find; This is an idempotent operation; patient 1..1 id; name 1..1 code

evidence.detail: The R4 example shows the operation as an HTTP GET returning a List resource body.
evidence.quote: GET /ehr/fhir/List/$find?patient=example&name=$current-allergies ... HTTP/1.1 200 OK ... <List xmlns="http://hl7.org/fhir">

evidence.detail: The fanout manifest classifies the shard as r4-only/unmatched with no R6 ids or files.
evidence.quote: List-find	r4-only	unmatched	List-find

evidence.detail: R4 rendered pages for list-operation-find.html and operation-list-find.html returned 200 and have local paths; the corresponding R6 ballot4 URLs returned 404.
evidence.quote: r4-4.0.1	list-operation-find.html	...	200; r6-6.0.0-ballot4	list-operation-find.html	...	404

evidence.detail: Package glob checks found no R6 List-find OperationDefinition and no R6 OperationDefinition with find in the file name.
The R4 operations list includes the List find route.
evidence.quote: Find a functional list[base]/List/$find

evidence.detail: The R6 operations list includes the resource-type operation table but has no List $find row; a direct search for list-operation-find, [base]/List, and $find in the R6 operations list found no matches.
The R4 base CapabilityStatement advertises a REST operation named find for the List find definition.
evidence.quote: find	http://hl7.org/fhir/OperationDefinition/list-find

evidence.detail: The R6 base CapabilityStatement rest.operation list omits find/list-find while advertising other operations such as versions, lookup, validate-code, translate, docref, evaluate, purge, events, status, expand, and validate-code.
R6 migration context: the special _list SearchParameter remains available for resources referenced by a List resource or a predefined functional list.
evidence.quote: "description":"Allows for the retrieval of resources that are referenced by a List resource or by one of the pre-defined functional lists"

evidence.detail: The R6 search narrative says _list values may be a List id or a functional-list literal and says servers need not expose functional lists as List resources.
evidence.quote: Input values are treated as token values - either the logical identifier (id) of a List or a literal for a functional list ... servers are not required to make the lists available to the clients as List resources

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The runtime mechanism is route and contract disappearance. An R4 client can call `[base]/List/$find` with required `patient` and `name` inputs and expect either a `List` response body or 404. In R6 there is no base OperationDefinition, rendered operation page, operations-list entry, or base CapabilityStatement advertisement for that route, so generated clients may lack a method, generated servers may lack a route, and validators/conformance tests generated from R6 will not know the R4 parameter schema.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Treat `List/$find` as a legacy/local operation when moving to R6. Servers that still support the R4 behavior should publish an implementation-guide or local OperationDefinition using the R4 canonical or a clearly versioned local canonical and advertise it explicitly in CapabilityStatement. Clients should use CapabilityStatement feature detection and should not assume all R6 servers support this route. If the workflow only needs resources in a functional list, use `_list` search with the functional-list literal plus ordinary search criteria. If the workflow specifically needs the `List` resource instance for a functional list, migration may require a server-specific route, a local operation, or direct List search only on servers that choose to expose those functional lists as List resources.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: remove a draft, FMM 1, trial-use operation that duplicates part of functional-list search behavior and whose own R4 narrative says servers may support searching by functional list without supporting the direct operation. The same goal could have been met only partially with a less-breaking base design: keeping a retired or explicitly legacy OperationDefinition in the R6 package while removing it from the base CapabilityStatement would preserve canonical/tooling continuity, but would also keep surfacing a low-maturity route that R6 appears to have intentionally dropped. Because the operation is low maturity and a search-based path remains for many use cases, the hard removal is more acceptable than it would be for a mature, widely implemented operation.

findings.title: R6 replaces the R4 topic/subject request contract with required measureUrl and status inputs

changedFields.note: The R6 formal package uses `reporter` and `reporterResource`; the rendered R6 operation pages show `organization` and `organizationResource` instead, which is captured separately as a narrative inconsistency.
R4 requires a subject; R6 allows the server to decide evaluated subjects if neither subject nor subjectGroup is supplied.

parameterDeltas.name: measureUrl
parameterDeltas.impactMd: A conformant R6 request must include one or more measure canonical URLs. R4 requests that selected measures only by `topic` do not satisfy the formal R6 contract.

parameterDeltas.name: status
parameterDeltas.impactMd: A conformant R6 request must include at least one gap status. R4 clients had no required status selector and would be rejected by validators or servers that enforce the R6 OperationDefinition.

parameterDeltas.name: topic
parameterDeltas.impactMd: R4 clients used `topic` as the required measure selection mechanism. The formal R6 package no longer defines that parameter, so generated R6 clients and server validators may reject or ignore it.

parameterDeltas.name: subject

oldValue.documentation: Subject for which the care gaps report will be produced

newValue.documentation: Subject may be Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, Location, Device, or Group; if omitted the subjects evaluated are server-defined; cannot be used with subjectGroup.

parameterDeltas.impactMd: Reverse-direction compatibility notes omitted; this report is scoped to R4→R6 compatibility.

parameterDeltas.name: subjectGroup
parameterDeltas.impactMd: Reverse-direction compatibility notes omitted; this report is scoped to R4→R6 compatibility.

parameterDeltas.name: practitioner
parameterDeltas.impactMd: Additive R6 provider-scoped filtering has no R4 formal counterpart.

parameterDeltas.name: location
parameterDeltas.impactMd: Additive R6 location filtering has no R4 formal counterpart.

parameterDeltas.name: reporter
parameterDeltas.impactMd: Additive R6 reporter filtering has no R4 formal counterpart and is also subject to the rendered-page/package naming inconsistency described in a separate finding.

parameterDeltas.name: reporterResource
parameterDeltas.impactMd: Additive R6 contained-resource style reporter input has no R4 formal counterpart and is also subject to the rendered-page/package naming inconsistency described in a separate finding.

parameterDeltas.name: isDocument
parameterDeltas.impactMd: Reverse-direction compatibility notes omitted; this report is scoped to R4→R6 compatibility.

parameterDeltas.name: parameters
parameterDeltas.impactMd: Additive R6 CQL input Parameters support has no R4 formal counterpart.

parameterDeltas.name: manifest
parameterDeltas.impactMd: Additive R6 dependency-resolution manifest support has no R4 formal counterpart.

findings.matchRationaleMd: The artifacts have the same canonical URL `http://hl7.org/fhir/OperationDefinition/Measure-care-gaps`, the same operation code `care-gaps`, and the same `Measure` type-level invocation flags, so this is a same-operation contract change rather than a rename or replacement.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 clients that send the R4 documented request (`periodStart`, `periodEnd`, `topic`, and a subject reference) are missing two required formal R6 inputs: `measureUrl` and `status`. Generated clients, server request validators, and conformance tests based on the R6 OperationDefinition will also stop recognizing `topic` as a formal input.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `Measure-care-gaps` is standards-status `trial-use` and FMM 2. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A payer or provider quality-measure client built from R4 calls `GET [base]/Measure/$care-gaps?periodStart=2014&periodEnd=2014&topic=Preventive%20Care%20and%20Screening&subject=Patient/123`. A strict R6 server or generated SDK rejects the request because `measureUrl` and `status` are required and `topic` is not a formal input.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: R6 could have added `measureUrl`, status filtering, and the richer provider/group/context parameters while retaining `topic` as a deprecated or alternate selector and defaulting omitted `status` to all defined gap statuses. The base invariant could require either the legacy `topic` selector or the newer measure identifier/canonical selector, rather than making `measureUrl` and `status` unconditionally required.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: This would preserve most R4 requests but would leave multiple measure-selection modes in the base operation, require precedence rules when both `topic` and `measureUrl` are supplied, and make an omitted status less explicit. Those tradeoffs are real, but they appear modest compared with rejecting the documented R4 request shape outright.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The R6 goal of more precise measure selection and explicit gap status filtering is reasonable. The concern is the same canonical endpoint becoming incompatible with the R4 required request shape when a plausible transition-compatible base contract could have accepted legacy `topic` requests and defaulted status behavior.

evidence.detail: R4 formal inputs are `periodStart` 1..1 date, `periodEnd` 1..1 date, `topic` 1..1 string, and `subject` 1..1 string reference.
evidence.quote: "parameter":[{"name":"periodStart"...},{"name":"periodEnd"...},{"name":"topic","use":"in","min":1,"max":"1"...},{"name":"subject","use":"in","min":1,"max":"1"...}]

evidence.detail: R6 formal inputs add required `measureUrl` 1..* canonical and required `status` 1..* code, remove formal `topic`, and make `subject` optional.
evidence.quote: "measureUrl" 1..* canonical; "subject" 0..1 string reference; "status" 1..* code

evidence.detail: R4 rendered operation page shows `topic` and `subject` as required input parameters.
evidence.quote: topic 1..1 string ... subject 1..1 string (reference)

evidence.detail: R6 rendered operation page shows required `measureUrl` and `status`, optional `subject`, and many added context parameters.
evidence.quote: measureUrl 1..* canonical ... subject 0..1 ... status 1..* code

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The operation code and endpoint path remain the same, so clients are likely to call the same URL with the R4 parameter names. R6 OperationDefinition-driven routers, validators, generated clients, and conformance tests will treat a request without `measureUrl` and `status` as invalid and may treat `topic` as unknown.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6, populate `measureUrl` with one or more Measure canonical URLs and include one or more `status` codes. Continue sending `periodStart` and `periodEnd`. Map R4 `topic` selection to explicit measure canonical URLs where possible; when the topic-to-measure mapping is server-defined, migration requires business logic or server-side compatibility support. Treat R6-only inputs as lossy when downgrading to R4.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The inferred R6 goal is stronger care-gap selection: canonical measure identity, explicit gap status, group/provider/location filtering, CQL parameters, and manifest-based dependency resolution. That goal is reasonable. A less-breaking base R6 design could have kept `topic` as an alternate or deprecated selector and made `status` default to all statuses when omitted, preserving most R4 requests while still allowing precise R6 clients to use `measureUrl` and explicit statuses. The tradeoff is a more complex selector matrix, but the current design imposes an immediate runtime and generated-code break under an unchanged canonical operation.

findings.title: R6 changes successful responses from a direct Bundle to Parameters containing repeated return Bundles

changedFields.note: The repeated return parameter means the operation no longer qualifies for the R4 direct-resource response shape.

changedFields.oldValue: Direct Bundle response for the only out parameter named `return`.
changedFields.newValue: Parameters resource containing zero or more `return` parameters whose resources are Bundles.
changedFields.note: The R6 operation page explicitly says the repeated `return` parameter is returned using `Parameters` even if the result is a single Bundle.

parameterDeltas.name: return

oldValue.documentation: The result of the care gaps report will be returned as a document bundle with a MeasureReport entry for each included measure

newValue.documentation: The $care-gaps operation returns zero or more document Bundles, one for each input subject.

parameterDeltas.impactMd: R4 clients that deserialize HTTP 200 responses directly as `Bundle` will fail against a conformant R6 server that returns a `Parameters` resource.

parameterDeltas.name: return
parameterDeltas.oldValue: R4 documented one document Bundle with a MeasureReport entry for each included measure.
parameterDeltas.newValue: R6 documents zero or more document Bundles, one for each input subject, and says a `Parameters` response is used even for a single Bundle.
parameterDeltas.impactMd: The operation result semantics changed from one aggregate document response to a potentially empty or multi-document response.

findings.matchRationaleMd: The response delta occurs within the same canonical operation matched by URL and code; it is not a new operation.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The response body's top-level resource type changes for conformant R6 servers from `Bundle` to `Parameters`. This is a hard runtime break for clients, SDK method signatures, validators, mock servers, and conformance tests expecting a direct Bundle.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `Measure-care-gaps` is standards-status `trial-use` and FMM 2. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A generated R4 client method returns `Bundle` for `$care-gaps`. Against an R6 server it receives `Parameters`, so deserialization fails before application code can inspect the contained document Bundles.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: R6 could have allowed the R4 direct `Bundle` response when exactly one Bundle is produced and used `Parameters` only for zero or multiple returned Bundles. Another partial design would preserve a single aggregate Bundle response for one-subject requests while introducing a separate repeated-output mode for multi-subject requests.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: These designs preserve the common single-result R4 path but create a dual response shape that R6 clients must handle and that conformance tests must specify carefully. The current single `Parameters` envelope is cleaner for multiple results, but forcing it even for one result breaks the R4 direct-response behavior more than necessary.

freshReview.rationaleMd: Supporting multiple document Bundles is a reasonable R6 goal. The concern is the mandatory envelope switch even when only a single Bundle is returned; a transitional direct-Bundle allowance could have preserved most R4 clients while still permitting the multi-Bundle R6 case.

evidence.detail: R4 `return` is the only out parameter, required, single, and type Bundle.
evidence.quote: "name":"return","use":"out","min":1,"max":"1"..."type":"Bundle"

evidence.detail: R4 operation page states the only `return` resource is returned directly.
evidence.quote: Note: as this is the only out parameter, it is a resource, and it has the name 'return', the result of this operation is returned directly as a resource

evidence.detail: R6 `return` is optional and repeatable with type Bundle.
evidence.quote: "name":"return","use":"out","min":0,"max":"*"..."type":"Bundle"

evidence.detail: R6 operation page states repeated `return` Bundles are returned using a Parameters resource even if only one Bundle is present.
evidence.quote: even though there is a single parameter named return of type Bundle, it is a multi-cardinality parameter, and so will still be returned using a Parameters resource

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: Operation response dispatch changes at the top-level resource type. R4 callers, generated clients, and validators expect `Bundle`; R6 formal behavior requires `Parameters` with repeated `return` entries, so a successful HTTP response can be syntactically valid FHIR but rejected by old client code.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: R6 clients should parse the response as `Parameters` and collect every `parameter` whose `name` is `return` and whose resource is a `Bundle`. Servers offering compatibility for R4 clients need a negotiated or version-specific mode that returns a direct Bundle for the single-result case.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The inferred R6 goal is to represent zero or more document Bundles, commonly one per subject. That goal is reasonable and may not fit the R4 single direct-Bundle response. However, the R6 design could have preserved the R4 response for the common exactly-one-Bundle case and used `Parameters` for zero/multiple results. The tradeoff is a less uniform R6 response contract, but the current design maximizes uniformity by imposing a hard response-envelope break even when no multiple-result capability is exercised.

findings.title: R6 rendered operation pages disagree with the formal R6 package for provider/selector parameters and examples

changedFields.note: This is an internal R6 package-versus-rendered-page mismatch, not a direct R4 package field.

changedFields.oldValue: Formal R6 package parameters do not include `measureId`, `measureIdentifier`, `topic`, `patient`, or `organization`.
changedFields.newValue: Rendered R6 examples use `measureId`, `measureIdentifier`, `topic`, `patient`, and `organization`.
changedFields.note: The examples include both R4-like and apparently intended R6 selector names that are not in the formal package OperationDefinition.

changedFields.oldValue: R6 package comment describes one or more Bundles and a Parameters response.
changedFields.newValue: Rendered R6 operation pages still include the older topic-based comment about calculating a set of measures for a topic.
changedFields.note: The formal computable comment and rendered narrative are not aligned.

parameterDeltas.name: reporter
parameterDeltas.path: R6 OperationDefinition.parameter[reporter] versus rendered page table
parameterDeltas.impactMd: An implementer using the package will generate `reporter`; an implementer using the rendered operation page or examples may send `organization`.

parameterDeltas.name: reporterResource
parameterDeltas.impactMd: The rendered page suggests a narrower Organization resource parameter, while the package defines a more general reporter resource parameter.

parameterDeltas.name: examples
parameterDeltas.oldValue: R4 examples use `topic` and `patient` and return a direct Bundle.
parameterDeltas.newValue: R6 examples use `measureUrl`, `measureId`, `measureIdentifier`, `topic`, `patient`, `subject`, `organization`, and direct Bundle responses, not all of which match the formal R6 package.
parameterDeltas.impactMd: Example-driven client or conformance-test authors can produce requests that do not validate against the formal R6 OperationDefinition.

findings.matchRationaleMd: The inconsistency was found while reviewing the same R6 canonical operation's package JSON and its two rendered operation pages.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is primarily a documentation/conformance risk, not a separate formal R4-to-R6 wire-contract change. It can still cause real failures because implementers often copy operation examples or page tables; requests using `organization`, `measureId`, `measureIdentifier`, `topic`, or `patient` may not pass formal R6 OperationDefinition validation unless servers add nonstandard aliases.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `Measure-care-gaps` is standards-status `trial-use` and FMM 2. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A conformance test author copies the R6 example using `measureId` or `organization`, while the server validates against the package OperationDefinition that requires `measureUrl` and defines `reporter` rather than `organization`; the test fails even though both sides followed an R6 source.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: Before publication, align the rendered pages and examples with the package OperationDefinition, or add the example parameter names as explicit formal aliases if they are intended to be valid.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: The tradeoff is editorial and design cleanup rather than a meaningful runtime burden. If aliases are added, the formal operation contract becomes broader but clearer.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The issue deserves revisit because it is avoidable and affects a same-operation normative ballot page. It should be resolved either by changing the formal OperationDefinition or by correcting the rendered narrative/examples.

evidence.detail: R6 package parameter list includes `reporter` and `reporterResource` but not `organization`, `organizationResource`, `measureId`, `measureIdentifier`, `topic`, or `patient`.
evidence.quote: reporter 0..1 string reference; reporterResource 0..1 Element reference

evidence.detail: R6 rendered operation documentation table uses `organization` and `organizationResource`.
evidence.quote: organization 0..1 string (reference) ... organizationResource 0..1 Organization

evidence.detail: R6 examples use query parameters that are absent from the formal R6 package, including `patient`, `measureId`, `measureIdentifier`, `topic`, and `organization`.
evidence.quote: GET [base]/Measure/$care-gaps?...measureId=EXM130-7.3.000...&topic=57024-2 ... &organization=Organization/124

evidence.detail: The rendered R6 OperationDefinition narrative keeps the older topic-based effect comment even though the package comment was updated for one-or-more Bundles and Parameters response.
evidence.quote: calculate a set of measures for a particular topic ... return a document describing the results of each measure for the given subject

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The strongest mechanism is documentation-driven mismatch: code generated from the package and code written from the page/examples can use different query parameter names for the same R6 operation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Treat the R6 package OperationDefinition as the formal contract unless a later ballot or erratum aligns the pages. Avoid using rendered-page-only parameter names in interoperable clients unless the target server explicitly documents aliases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The inferred goal is to document richer care-gaps invocation examples. That goal is reasonable, but it should be achieved with page examples that validate against the same formal OperationDefinition, or by formalizing the extra names as aliases. The current mismatch is not a necessary breaking base design and is likely an editorial or generation defect.

findings.title: Instance-level Measure/$collect-data invocation is removed

changedFields.note: R4 permitted `[base]/Measure/[id]/$collect-data`; R6 only permits the type-level Measure endpoint.
The rendered operation pages mirror the computable invocation flag change.

findings.matchRationaleMd: The R4 and R6 artifacts have the same canonical URL `http://hl7.org/fhir/OperationDefinition/Measure-collect-data`, operation code `collect-data`, and resource context `Measure`; the behavior change is inside that common operation.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 client can validly invoke `GET [base]/Measure/{id}/$collect-data` without a separate measure selector. A strict R6 server generated from the OperationDefinition can reject that URL, omit the instance route, or fail conformance tests that assert the R4 route. Generated SDKs and server routers also lose an operation method scoped to a Measure instance.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `Measure-collect-data` is standards-status `trial-use` and FMM 2. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A quality-reporting client calls `GET /Measure/measure-mrp/$collect-data?periodStart=2018&periodEnd=2018&subject=Patient/123` against an R6 server and receives 404 or an operation-not-supported error because only `/Measure/$collect-data` is implemented.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: Keep `instance: true` in R6 while adding the new type-level `measureUrl` contract. On an instance invocation, the server can infer the selected Measure from the URL and either ignore `measureUrl` or define a simple consistency rule if it is supplied.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: The tradeoff is continued support for the legacy route and a small amount of precedence/error handling, but it would preserve the R4 instance call while still enabling the R6 canonical multi-measure form.

freshReview.rationaleMd: Removing the instance route is a direct runtime break and the apparent R6 goal can be met without dropping it. The operation is now presented as normative/FMM 3, so this avoidable route removal deserves renewed review.

evidence.detail: R4 computable flags advertise type and instance invocation.
evidence.quote: "system":false,"type":true,"instance":true

evidence.detail: R6 computable flags retain type invocation but disable instance invocation and explicitly mark the operation non-state-changing.
evidence.quote: "affectsState":false,"code":"collect-data" ... "system":false,"type":true,"instance":false

evidence.detail: The R4 operation page lists both type and instance URLs.
evidence.quote: URL: [base]/Measure/$collect-data ... URL: [base]/Measure/[id]/$collect-data

evidence.detail: The R6 operation page lists only the type URL and states the operation is idempotent.
evidence.quote: URL: [base]/Measure/$collect-data ... This is an idempotent operation

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The REST path changes: R4 instance calls are no longer valid under the R6 OperationDefinition. Routers, generated server stubs, generated client methods, and conformance tests that key from `OperationDefinition.instance` will remove or reject `[base]/Measure/[id]/$collect-data`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move instance calls to the type-level endpoint and supply `measureUrl` for the Measure being collected. Servers that need to support mixed R4/R6 clients should consider a compatibility route for `[base]/Measure/[id]/$collect-data` and normalize it internally to the R6 `measureUrl` form.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The inferred R6 goal is to use canonical measure selection and support collection for measures independent of server-local ids. That goal is reasonable, but it did not require removing instance invocation. Preserving the instance route as an alias would keep most R4 clients working with modest server/router complexity.

findings.title: The `measure` selector is replaced by required repeatable `measureUrl` canonical values

changedFields.note: R6 removes the optional R4 local/reference selector and requires at least one canonical measure URL.

parameterDeltas.name: measure

oldValue.documentation: The measure to evaluate. This parameter is only required when the operation is invoked on the resource type, it is not used when invoking the operation on a Measure instance.

parameterDeltas.impactMd: R4 type-level clients that send `measure=Measure/{id}` or similar reference-style values have no computable R6 parameter with that name or type.

parameterDeltas.name: measureUrl

newValue.documentation: This the the URL of a measure for which the data-of-interest will be collected.

parameterDeltas.impactMd: Every R6 invocation must supply at least one canonical URL. That is stricter than R4 type-level calls and incompatible with R4 instance-level calls that inferred the measure from the URL.

findings.matchRationaleMd: The operation is the same canonical `$collect-data` operation, but the parameter used to identify the Measure changed name, type, cardinality, and repeatability.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Measure selection is central to this operation. R4 clients can omit the selector for instance invocations or send one optional `measure` reference for type invocations; R6 validators and generated clients require `measureUrl` `1..*` canonical. R6 requests with multiple canonical measure URLs also cannot be represented faithfully in the single optional R4 `measure` reference slot.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `Measure-collect-data` is standards-status `trial-use` and FMM 2. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: An R4 integration sends `GET /Measure/$collect-data?measure=Measure/measure-mrp&periodStart=2018&periodEnd=2018`; an R6 server generated from the OperationDefinition rejects the request because `measureUrl` is missing and `measure` is unknown.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: Add `measureUrl` as the preferred canonical, repeatable selector but retain `measure` as a deprecated optional single-reference alias. R6 could require at least one of `measure`, `measureUrl`, or the instance URL, with clear precedence and normalization rules.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: This keeps one legacy alias and requires servers to resolve a reference to a canonical when possible. The tradeoff is modest compared with rejecting established R4 requests.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The canonical selector goal is reasonable, but replacing the old selector and making the new one required is more breaking than necessary. A transitional alias would preserve most R4 requests while still steering new clients to canonical URLs.

evidence.detail: R4 defines the optional `measure` selector as a string reference.
evidence.quote: "name":"measure","use":"in","min":0,"max":"1" ... "type":"string","searchType":"reference"

evidence.detail: R4 narrative says the selector is only required on type invocation and not used on instance invocation.
evidence.quote: The measure to evaluate. This parameter is only required when the operation is invoked on the resource type, it is not used when invoking the operation on a Measure instance

evidence.detail: R6 defines `measureUrl` as required, repeatable, and canonical.
evidence.quote: "name":"measureUrl","use":"in","min":1,"max":"*" ... "type":"canonical"

evidence.detail: R6 narrative table confirms `measureUrl` cardinality `1..*` and type canonical.
evidence.quote: measureUrl ... 1..* ... canonical ... URL of a measure

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The wire parameter name, datatype, and minimum cardinality changed. Package-driven clients will expose `measureUrl` instead of `measure`; package-driven servers can reject R4 `measure` requests as unknown and reject any request that does not include a canonical URL.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Populate `measureUrl` from the Measure canonical URL, not the local resource id. When migrating R4 instance invocations, first resolve the Measure resource and use its canonical URL. Downgrading R6 calls with multiple `measureUrl` values to R4 requires splitting into multiple R4 calls or choosing one measure, which is lossy.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The inferred R6 goal is portable, canonical measure identification and support for multiple measures. That goal could have been achieved with a less-breaking base design that adds `measureUrl` while retaining the R4 `measure` alias for single-reference requests. The tradeoff is alias support and reference-to-canonical resolution, but no duplicate payload representation is required.

findings.title: The `practitioner` filter is removed in favor of broader reporter/provider parameters

changedFields.note: The R6 package generalizes provider attribution but does not retain the R4 `practitioner` parameter name.

parameterDeltas.name: practitioner

oldValue.documentation: Practitioner for which the measure will be collected.

parameterDeltas.impactMd: R4 clients that filter by `practitioner=Practitioner/{id}` have no computable R6 parameter with that name.

parameterDeltas.name: reporter

newValue.documentation: The provider for which the data-of-interest will be collected.

parameterDeltas.impactMd: `reporter` appears to be the closest string-reference replacement for `practitioner`, but it is broader and maps to MeasureReport.reporter rather than the R4 primary-practitioner collection language.

parameterDeltas.name: reporterResource
parameterDeltas.impactMd: R6 can carry provider resources not already on the server, which is not representable by the R4 `practitioner` string reference.

findings.matchRationaleMd: This is a parameter-level change within the same canonical operation, not a separate operation replacement.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The provider filter is optional, so clients that do not use it are unaffected. Clients and tests that do use R4 `practitioner` will fail against a strict R6 operation definition, and R6 reporter values for PractitionerRole or Organization cannot be reduced cleanly to an R4 practitioner filter.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `Measure-collect-data` is standards-status `trial-use` and FMM 2. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A payer quality reporting client sends `practitioner=Practitioner/abc` to collect data for a provider panel; an R6 server generated from the package ignores or rejects the unknown parameter and returns broader or failed results.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: Retain `practitioner` as a deprecated optional alias for `reporter` when the reference target is Practitioner, while adding `reporter` and `reporterResource` for the broader R6 provider-attribution use cases.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: The tradeoff is maintaining one legacy alias and documenting precedence if both are supplied. It does not block broader reporter semantics.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The broader provider-attribution goal is reasonable, but dropping the old optional parameter name is avoidable and risks silent behavior changes if unknown parameters are ignored.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `practitioner` as the provider filter.
evidence.quote: practitioner ... 0..1 ... string (reference) ... Practitioner for which the measure will be collected

evidence.detail: R6 package defines `reporter` and `reporterResource`, not `practitioner`.
evidence.quote: "name":"reporter" ... "type":"string","searchType":"reference" ... "name":"reporterResource" ... "type":"Element","searchType":"reference"

evidence.detail: The R6 package constrains reporterResource allowed resource types.
evidence.quote: operationdefinition-allowed-type ... Practitioner ... PractitionerRole ... Organization

evidence.detail: The rendered R6 operation page describes the broader reporter/provider semantics.
evidence.quote: reporter ... Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or Organization ... reflected in the reporter element ... reporterResource

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The R4 query parameter name disappears from the computable R6 contract. Generated client APIs and validators will expose `reporter` and `reporterResource`; servers generated from those definitions may treat `practitioner` as unknown. If a server ignores unknown parameters, the failure mode can be a broader data collection result rather than an explicit error.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map R4 `practitioner=Practitioner/{id}` to R6 `reporter=Practitioner/{id}` when the intended meaning is reporter/provider attribution. Use `reporterResource` only when the Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or Organization resource itself must be supplied. Test that servers reject or warn on stale `practitioner` rather than silently widening the result set.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The inferred R6 goal is to support provider attribution beyond an individual practitioner and to reflect the provider in resulting MeasureReports. That goal could have been achieved by adding `reporter` and `reporterResource` while preserving `practitioner` as a deprecated alias for the common Practitioner case. The tradeoff is small alias complexity and possible precedence rules.

findings.title: Output changes from `measureReport` plus `resource` parts to repeatable `return` Bundles

changedFields.note: The R6 response is still a Parameters resource because `return` is repeatable, but the named parts and resource organization are different.

changedFields.oldValue: A MeasureReport of type data-collection detailing the results of the operation
changedFields.newValue: The first entries in each Bundle are MeasureReport(s) ... The MeasureReport resources SHALL have a type of data-exchange.
changedFields.note: The operation-specific output text also changes the expected MeasureReport type code.

parameterDeltas.name: measureReport
parameterDeltas.impactMd: R4 response parsers expecting a required `measureReport` part will not find it in a conformant R6 response.

parameterDeltas.name: resource
parameterDeltas.impactMd: R4 response parsers expecting data-of-interest resources as top-level Parameters parts must now read Bundle entries.

parameterDeltas.name: return
parameterDeltas.impactMd: R6 returns one Bundle per input subject, so response processing and validation move from top-level OperationOutcome Parameters parts to Bundle structure.

parameterDeltas.name: MeasureReport.type
parameterDeltas.impactMd: Reverse-direction compatibility notes omitted; this report is scoped to R4→R6 compatibility.

findings.matchRationaleMd: The output change is within the same matched canonical operation and affects the operation-specific Parameters response shape.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Every successful invocation must parse the output. A strict R4 client looking for `measureReport` and `resource` top-level parts will not understand a conformant R6 response with repeatable Bundle `return` parts. Conversely, an R6 response with multiple per-subject Bundles, multiple measure reports, and data-exchange MeasureReports cannot be represented cleanly in the R4 output shape.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `Measure-collect-data` is standards-status `trial-use` and FMM 2. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A generated R4 client deserializes the `Parameters` response and asserts one `measureReport` part. Against R6 it receives `parameter.name=return` with a Bundle and fails to find the report unless it rewrites response traversal.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: R6 could have allowed optional legacy `measureReport` and `resource` output parts for single-measure/single-subject responses while adding `return` Bundle for the new multi-measure or per-subject structure.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: That preserves common simple cases but creates duplicate representations, ambiguous precedence, and incomplete coverage for the multi-measure/per-subject goal. It would also make conformance tests more complex because servers could choose old or new output shapes.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The break is real and broad for implementers of this operation, but the old output shape is a poor fit for the R6 goal of returning organized Bundles per subject and supporting multiple measures. A less-breaking design exists only for simple cases and carries material interoperability tradeoffs.

evidence.detail: R4 output parameters are `measureReport` and `resource`.
evidence.quote: "name":"measureReport","use":"out","min":1,"max":"1" ... "type":"MeasureReport" ... "name":"resource","use":"out","min":0,"max":"*" ... "type":"Resource"

evidence.detail: R4 narrative describes the old output shape and MeasureReport type.
evidence.quote: measureReport ... 1..1 ... MeasureReport ... A MeasureReport of type data-collection ... resource ... 0..* ... Resource

evidence.detail: R6 package defines a repeatable Bundle `return` output.
evidence.quote: "name":"return","use":"out","min":0,"max":"*" ... "type":"Bundle"

evidence.detail: R6 narrative describes Bundle output and data-exchange MeasureReports.
evidence.quote: return ... 0..* ... Bundle ... MeasureReport resources SHALL have a type of data-exchange ... still be returned using a Parameters resource

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The response `Parameters` names and resource nesting changed. Generated response models and validation tests keyed to `measureReport` and `resource` top-level parts must instead traverse repeatable `return` parts containing Bundles, then inspect entries for MeasureReport and data-of-interest resources.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update clients to iterate over all `return` Bundles, expect MeasureReport entries first, then follow `MeasureReport.evaluatedResource` references to Bundle entries. Update servers to produce a Bundle per input subject and to use the R6 operation-required MeasureReport type. Downgrading to R4 may require flattening Bundle entries and selecting or synthesizing a single MeasureReport, which is lossy for multi-measure or multi-subject results.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 output goal is plausible: a per-subject Bundle can organize MeasureReports and evaluated resources more cleanly and supports repeated `measureUrl` inputs. A partial less-breaking design could retain the old output parts for simple cases, but that would introduce duplicate output representations and would not solve the multi-measure/per-subject case. The breaking design is therefore probably proportionate, provided the migration path is clearly documented.

findings.title: R6 rendered pages mix stale and undeclared parameter names with the computable definition

changedFields.oldValue: Not applicable
changedFields.newValue: The R6 package has reporterResource as Element with allowed types Practitioner, PractitionerRole, and Organization, but the rendered pages show reporterResource as string/reference and also show organizationResource, which is absent from the package parameter array.
changedFields.note: This is an inconsistency between R6 primary inputs, not an R4 package field.

changedFields.oldValue: R4 examples use instance invocation and `measureReport` output.
changedFields.newValue: R6 examples include `measureId`, `measureIdentifier`, `organization`, and `practitioner` query parameters that are not defined by the R6 package OperationDefinition, and the example response still uses `measureReport` even though the R6 package output is `return` Bundle.
changedFields.note: The examples can lead page-driven implementers to send parameters that package-driven servers reject.

parameterDeltas.name: organizationResource
parameterDeltas.impactMd: `organizationResource` appears in the R6 rendered page but not in the R6 package OperationDefinition, creating conflicting client/server expectations.

parameterDeltas.name: measureId
parameterDeltas.newValue: Example request parameter not present in the R6 package OperationDefinition.
parameterDeltas.impactMd: Clients copying examples can send `measureId` even though the computable contract requires `measureUrl`.

parameterDeltas.name: measureReport
parameterDeltas.newValue: Example response parameter conflicts with the package output parameter `return`.
parameterDeltas.impactMd: The response example reinforces the R4 output name even though the R6 parameter table says the output is `return` Bundle.

findings.matchRationaleMd: This finding is tied to the same matched operation because the R6 rendered operation pages and R6 package artifact describe different parameter surfaces for `Measure/$collect-data`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an additional computable R4-to-R6 package break, but it is a practical R6 implementation risk. Page-driven clients may implement stale example parameters and fail against package-driven servers; package-driven validators and rendered-page conformance tests may disagree about accepted parameters.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `Measure-collect-data` is standards-status `trial-use` and FMM 2. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: An implementer follows the R6 operation page examples and sends `measureId` plus `practitioner`; a server generated from the R6 package rejects the request because `measureUrl` is required and `practitioner` is undeclared.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: Either update the R6 rendered pages and examples to use only computable parameters (`measureUrl`, `reporter` or `reporterResource`, and `return` Bundle), or add the documented legacy/example parameter names to the OperationDefinition as explicit aliases with deprecation guidance.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Pure editorial alignment has minimal tradeoff. If the stale names are intentional aliases, adding them to the computable definition increases alias support but makes client/server behavior explicit.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The inconsistency is avoidable and likely to produce implementation divergence. It should be revisited separately from the substantive package-level design changes.
