Maturity/status context for this R4 operation.
evidence.quote: "StructureDefinition-questionnaire": { "r4": { "id": "StructureDefinition-questionnaire", "url": "http://hl7.org/fhir/OperationDefinition/StructureDefinition-questionnaire", "name": "Build Questionnaire", "status": "draft", "standardsStatus": "trial-use", "fmm": 5 } }

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: At runtime, the removal affects both route discovery and invocation. An R4 client can call `[base]/StructureDefinition/$questionnaire` with `identifier`, `profile`, or `url`, or `[base]/StructureDefinition/{id}/$questionnaire` with selectors ignored, and can expect a directly returned `Questionnaire` resource on success. In R6 there is no base OperationDefinition for these routes, no standard Parameters schema to validate a request or response, and no core CapabilityStatement advertisement. Generated SDKs may drop a typed method, validators may reject the R4 operation invocation as unknown in R6, and servers that remove the endpoint will return unknown-operation or 404-like failures.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Clients should not assume `StructureDefinition/$questionnaire` exists on R6 servers. Use CapabilityStatement feature detection and prefer pre-authored Questionnaires, implementation-guide-specific questionnaire generation services, or local tooling that consumes StructureDefinitions outside the FHIR operation surface. Servers that need to support R4 clients can keep `$questionnaire` as a legacy/local operation with the R4 parameter contract and advertise it explicitly in their own CapabilityStatement, while making clear it is not a base R6 operation. Conformance tests should treat the operation as version-specific: expected for R4 only when advertised, not required or defined by R6 core.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: However, the same goal could have been met with a less-breaking base R6 design by retaining the canonical OperationDefinition as deprecated or retired, preserving `code: questionnaire`, the type/instance invocation declarations, and the parameter names, while removing it from the base CapabilityStatement and warning that IG-specific alternatives are preferred. The tradeoff is extra legacy surface and possible confusion, but it is less disruptive than deleting the operation from a FMM 5 trial-use artifact with no direct replacement.

findings.title: R6 changes StructureDefinition $snapshot from rendered non-idempotent to computably read-only/idempotent

changedFields.note: The R4 OperationDefinition file omits `affectsState` and the rendered R4 operation page says the operation is not idempotent; R6 sets `affectsState: false`.

changedFields.oldValue: This is not an idempotent operation
changedFields.newValue: This is an idempotent operation
changedFields.note: The operation-specific rendered page changes the advertised HTTP/idempotence semantics.

changedFields.oldValue: No snapshot-dependency or frozen-package idempotence caveat after the shared parameter-selection prose.
changedFields.newValue: Snapshot generation is dependent on profiles that are referenced - if those profiles change, the snapshot can change. For a frozen package, $snapshot is idempotent.
changedFields.note: R6 clarifies that the operation is read-only but its result can vary if external profile dependencies change.

findings.matchRationaleMd: The R4 and R6 OperationDefinitions have the same canonical URL, id, operation code, resource context, and type/instance invocation flags. This is a direct canonical-url match, not a replacement.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 clients that invoke `$snapshot` with POST remain compatible with R6. The practical risk is for R6 clients, generated operation stubs, routing layers, caches, or conformance tests that infer from `affectsState: false` that GET is allowed or expected for URL-only or instance-level calls. An R4-derived server that only implemented POST could fail those R6 expectations. The operation is mainly used by FHIR tooling, validators, and profile servers rather than ordinary clinical exchange, so runtime prevalence is occasional and severity is low, but the operation is FMM 5/normative in R6, making the conformance signal more important.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `StructureDefinition-snapshot` is standards-status `trial-use` and FMM 5. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A validator or package-registry client generated from R6 metadata calls `GET /StructureDefinition/$snapshot?url=http://example.org/StructureDefinition/my-profile`; an R4-derived profile server that only routed POST `$snapshot` returns `405 Method Not Allowed`, causing an R6 conformance or integration test failure.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: R6 could have left `affectsState` unset or kept the rendered operation as non-idempotent while adding only narrative guidance that snapshot generation is deterministic for frozen packages. A narrower alternative would be to mark `affectsState: false` but add operation-specific prose saying GET support is optional for `$snapshot` because of the optional resource-valued `definition` input.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Those alternatives would reduce pressure on POST-only R4 implementations, but they would also lose the computable read-only signal that generic clients and conformance tooling use, and they would preserve or deepen the R4 inconsistency where the page said non-idempotent while showing a GET example. Keeping POST support while adding GET/read-only semantics is a proportionate migration burden.

freshReview.rationaleMd: This is a real operation-runtime and conformance change, especially for servers that did not implement GET for `$snapshot`. It is probably acceptable because it is a widening/read-only clarification, not a removal of POST or a parameter-shape break, and the R6 narrative explains the only meaningful caveat: results are stable only when referenced profile inputs are stable.

evidence.detail: R4 operation has the same canonical URL/code/context and omits `affectsState`.
evidence.quote: "url":"http://hl7.org/fhir/OperationDefinition/StructureDefinition-snapshot" ... "code":"snapshot" ... "system":false,"type":true,"instance":true

evidence.detail: R6 operation sets the computable side-effect flag to false while keeping the same canonical URL/code/context.
evidence.quote: "affectsState":false,"code":"snapshot","resource":["StructureDefinition"],"system":false,"type":true,"instance":true

evidence.detail: R4 rendered operation page describes the same endpoints and says the operation is not idempotent.
evidence.quote: URL: [base]/StructureDefinition/$snapshot ... URL: [base]/StructureDefinition/[id]/$snapshot ... This is not an idempotent operation

evidence.detail: R6 rendered operation page adds dependency/idempotence caveat and says the operation is idempotent.
evidence.quote: Snapshot generation is dependent on profiles that are referenced - if those profiles change, the snapshot can change. For a frozen package, $snapshot is idempotent. ... This is an idempotent operation

evidence.detail: R6 general operation rules tie `affectsState=false` to GET invocation when compatible parameters are passed.
evidence.quote: Operations MAY be invoked using a GET ... if ... the operation does not affect the state of the server ... Servers SHALL support this method of invocation.

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The wire operation name and POST request/response shape are unchanged, so existing R4 clients should continue to work against R6 servers. The behavior change is in generic operation handling: R6 metadata says `$snapshot` does not affect server state, and the operation page renders it as idempotent. Generic R6 clients or test suites may therefore use or require GET for calls that can be represented in the URL, such as instance-level `$snapshot` with no input body or type-level `$snapshot?url=...`. Calls carrying the `definition` resource still require POST because that input cannot be represented as simple URL parameters.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Keep supporting POST for all `$snapshot` invocations. R6 servers should also route GET for the idempotent cases they can represent safely, especially instance-level `[base]/StructureDefinition/[id]/$snapshot` and type-level URL lookup. Clients that need to interoperate with R4 or mixed-version servers should continue to use POST unless the server version/capability behavior is known. Do not cache or compare snapshots across changing dependency packages; R6's idempotence statement is explicitly for a frozen dependency set.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 goal is reasonable: `$snapshot` computes a representation and should not mutate server state, and making this computable helps generic clients, caches, and conformance tooling. A less-breaking base design could have preserved R4's rendered non-idempotent status and added only narrative text about stable inputs, or made GET support operation-specific and optional. That would reduce migration work for POST-only servers but would leave clients without a reliable computable read-only signal and retain the confusing R4 mismatch between the non-idempotence statement and the GET example. The chosen R6 design is mildly breaking for some server/test setups but proportionate.

findings.title: R6 scopes url, valueSet, and valueSetVersion to type-level invocation

changedFields.note: R6 makes the canonical URL input explicitly type-level.
R6 makes the inline ValueSet input explicitly type-level.
R6 makes the value set version selector explicitly type-level.

parameterDeltas.name: url
parameterDeltas.impactMd: Type-level `[base]/ValueSet/$expand` calls are unchanged. Instance-level calls that redundantly send `url` can be rejected by R6 OperationDefinition-driven validators because the instance URL already supplies the ValueSet context.

parameterDeltas.name: valueSet
parameterDeltas.impactMd: Inline ValueSet expansion remains available at type level. R6 clients and server stubs generated from the OperationDefinition should not offer this parameter on `[base]/ValueSet/[id]/$expand`.

parameterDeltas.name: valueSetVersion
parameterDeltas.impactMd: An R4-era client that used `valueSetVersion` on an instance-level URL may need to move to type-level canonical invocation or rely on the instance/version selected by the server.

findings.matchRationaleMd: The R4 and R6 artifacts have the same canonical URL, id, operation code `expand`, and ValueSet resource context. The scoped-parameter delta is assessed as a change within the matched operation.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The endpoint surface is unchanged, and R4 already described `url`, `context`, or `valueSet` as needed when the operation is not called at instance level. The new risk is that R6 makes three parameters computably unavailable on instance-level invocation, so generated clients, validators, or conformance tests can reject redundant request shapes that an R4 implementation may have tolerated.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `ValueSet-expand` is standards-status `normative` and FMM 5. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A generated R6 SDK exposes separate method signatures for type-level and instance-level `$expand`; an integration test that still sends `valueSetVersion` with `/ValueSet/123/$expand` fails validation even though an R4 server ignored or accepted the extra parameter.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: R6 could have scoped these parameters to both type and instance levels and defined precedence rules when the instance URL conflicts with `url` or an inline `valueSet`.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: That would preserve redundant R4-tolerated calls, but it would leave ambiguous requests in the base operation and make generated APIs handle conflicting ValueSet identities. The type-only scope is a reasonable way to make the invocation contract explicit.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The change can break narrow generated-code or validator workflows, but it formalizes a distinction already present in the R4 prose and avoids conflicting source-of-ValueSet inputs on instance invocation.

evidence.detail: R4 has no OperationDefinition.parameter.scope entries for url, valueSet, or valueSetVersion.
evidence.quote: R4 parameters include url 0..1 uri, valueSet 0..1 ValueSet, and valueSetVersion 0..1 string without scope metadata.

evidence.detail: R6 gives url, valueSet, and valueSetVersion scope type.
evidence.quote: url type; valueSet type; valueSetVersion type

evidence.detail: R6 defines parameter.scope as applying when the operation is invoked at the specified level.
evidence.quote: If present, indicates that the parameter applies when the operation is being invoked at the specified level.

evidence.detail: The R6 rendered operation page adds a Scope column and shows type for url, valueSet, and valueSetVersion.
evidence.quote: Name | Scope | Cardinality ... url | type | 0..1 ... valueSet | type | 0..1 ... valueSetVersion | type | 0..1

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: OperationDefinition-driven validators and SDK generators can now distinguish type-level-only inputs from inputs available on both ValueSet invocation levels. That affects method signatures and request validation even though the REST URLs are unchanged.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Use `url`, `valueSet`, and `valueSetVersion` with `[base]/ValueSet/$expand`. For `[base]/ValueSet/[id]/$expand`, rely on the instance URL to identify the ValueSet and avoid sending type-scoped source parameters unless the server explicitly documents legacy tolerance.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: remove ambiguity about which ValueSet is being expanded. A less-breaking design could have allowed redundant parameters at instance level, but would need precedence rules and would preserve conflicting request shapes in the base operation. The chosen R6 design is a narrow compatibility break with a defensible computability benefit.

findings.title: R6 makes several existing $expand parameter and output semantics more enforceable

changedFields.oldValue: Controls whether or not the value set expansion nests codes or not.
changedFields.newValue: If excludeNested is true, the expansion MUST be flat; if false/default, nesting is possible but not required.
changedFields.note: R6 turns a previously terse control into a testable server obligation when true.

changedFields.oldValue: Controls whether the expansion is assembled for user interface use, with examples based on abstract codes and navigation groups.
changedFields.newValue: Defines concrete categories to exclude when true: notSelectable CodeSystem concepts, nested contains with no code, and abstract nested contains.
changedFields.note: R6 makes the existing UI-oriented flag more precise and may change output content for servers that used a different interpretation.

changedFields.oldValue: Controls whether the value set definition is included or excluded in value set expansions.
changedFields.newValue: Specifies that all ValueSet elements are included except expansion-specific id/meta and with the expansion filled out.
changedFields.note: R6 clarifies the returned ValueSet content when the existing flag is used.

changedFields.oldValue: No rule requiring definition ValueSet.status and ValueSet.version to be persisted into the expansion resource.
changedFields.newValue: When available, ValueSet.status and ValueSet.version from the definition SHALL be persisted to the expansion ValueSet.
changedFields.note: R6 adds an operation-level output metadata requirement without changing the formal return type.

parameterDeltas.name: excludeNested
parameterDeltas.oldValue: Controls whether or not the value set expansion nests codes or not.
parameterDeltas.newValue: If excludeNested is set to true, the expansion MUST be flat; if false/default, nesting is possible but not required.
parameterDeltas.impactMd: R6 conformance tests can now fail a server that returns nested `ValueSet.expansion.contains.contains` while `excludeNested=true`.

parameterDeltas.name: excludeNotForUI
parameterDeltas.oldValue: R4 described a UI/non-UI distinction with abstract-code examples and left exact implications to the code system.
parameterDeltas.newValue: R6 says `excludeNotForUI=true` excludes notSelectable concepts, contains entries with no code, and abstract nested contains.
parameterDeltas.impactMd: Servers with a different R4 interpretation may need to change expansion filtering for validation and code-generation use cases.

parameterDeltas.name: includeDefinition
parameterDeltas.oldValue: Controls whether the value set definition is included or excluded.
parameterDeltas.newValue: Includes all elements of the ValueSet except expansion-specific id/meta, with the expansion itself filled out.
parameterDeltas.impactMd: R6 narrows ambiguity for clients that request definitions in expansion responses; servers may need to include more complete definition content.

findings.matchRationaleMd: The matched operation keeps the same identity and parameter names; this finding covers changed normative prose on existing parameters and output metadata.

impact.impactRationaleMd: These changes do not invalidate existing R4 request serialization. They can, however, change response content and server conformance expectations for common `$expand` options used by UI, validation, and generated-code workflows.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `ValueSet-expand` is standards-status `normative` and FMM 5. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A terminology server that accepted `excludeNested=true` but still returned a hierarchy passes an R4 smoke test but fails an R6 conformance test that checks for a flat expansion; another server must copy the definition ValueSet version into the expansion resource for auditability.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: R6 could have used SHOULD-level language for flat expansions and status/version propagation, or left `excludeNotForUI` as server-discretion prose.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Those alternatives would reduce server conformance pressure but would not provide the same predictable behavior for clients that request flat, validation-oriented, or traceable expansions.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The changes create real conformance work for R4 servers, but the goals are reasonable and tied to predictable expansion results. The less-breaking alternatives mostly weaken computability rather than preserving an equally interoperable contract.

evidence.detail: R4 describes includeDefinition, excludeNested, excludeNotForUI, and paging/result behavior with less specific language.
evidence.quote: Controls whether or not the value set expansion nests codes or not ... Controls whether or not the value set expansion is assembled for a user interface use or not.

evidence.detail: R6 clarifies includeDefinition and adds enforceable excludeNested/excludeNotForUI details.
evidence.quote: If excludeNested is set to true, the expansion MUST be flat ... If excludeNotForUI is set to true, the concepts as described above will be excluded from the expansion.

evidence.detail: R6 keeps return 1..1 ValueSet and adds the status/version persistence rule in operation prose.
evidence.quote: When available, ValueSet.status and ValueSet.version from the ValueSet resource instance which contains the definition SHALL be persisted to the ValueSet resource instance which contains the expansion.

evidence.detail: The same changed prose appears in the computable OperationDefinition documentation/comment fields.
evidence.quote: If excludeNested is set to true, the expansion MUST be flat ... ValueSet.status and ValueSet.version ... SHALL be persisted.

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The formal parameter cardinalities and return type do not change, but servers that generate expansions can now be judged against more specific operation prose. That affects conformance tests, response diff tests, validators that inspect expansion shape, and downstream code-generation workflows that rely on flat or non-UI expansions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6, ensure `excludeNested=true` produces no nested `contains`, apply `excludeNotForUI=true` to the concrete R6 categories, populate requested definition content consistently with the R6 includeDefinition text, and propagate definition `ValueSet.status` and `ValueSet.version` into expansion resources when available. R4 clients should tolerate the additional metadata because it is carried in the returned ValueSet resource.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The inferred R6 goal is stronger interoperability of expansion outputs. A less-breaking base design could have preserved more server discretion, but that would not give clients a reliable flat/non-UI expansion contract or metadata traceability. The break is therefore proportionate even though the operation is mature normative content.

findings.title: R6 terminology-service narrative adds a required-support table for ValueSet-expand that may conflict with paging-optional operation prose

changedFields.note: R6 adds a terminology-service operations table that did not appear in the reviewed R4 terminology-service page.

changedFields.oldValue: Servers are not obliged to support paging, but if they do, SHALL support both offset and count.
changedFields.newValue: The R6 operation page retains the same paging-optional prose, while the terminology-service table lists offset and count as required input parameters.
changedFields.note: This creates uncertainty about whether R6 terminology services must support paging parameters despite the operation page saying paging is optional.

parameterDeltas.name: url
parameterDeltas.oldValue: No R4 terminology-service required-support table found in the reviewed page.
parameterDeltas.newValue: Listed in the R6 ValueSet-expand required input parameters column.
parameterDeltas.impactMd: A terminology-service conformance suite may require canonical URL expansion support as part of the baseline service contract.

parameterDeltas.name: filter
parameterDeltas.oldValue: R4 described filter as optional server-discretion behavior.
parameterDeltas.newValue: Listed in the R6 ValueSet-expand required input parameters column.
parameterDeltas.impactMd: Terminology servers may need to support text filtering for baseline R6 terminology-service conformance.

parameterDeltas.name: offset
parameterDeltas.oldValue: R4 operation prose said servers are not obliged to support paging.
parameterDeltas.newValue: Listed in the R6 ValueSet-expand required input parameters column.
parameterDeltas.impactMd: This is potentially breaking for R4 servers that did not implement paging and assumed that was allowed by the operation definition.

parameterDeltas.name: count
parameterDeltas.oldValue: R4 operation prose said servers are not obliged to support paging.
parameterDeltas.newValue: Listed in the R6 ValueSet-expand required input parameters column.
parameterDeltas.impactMd: This is potentially breaking for R4 servers that did not implement paging and assumed that was allowed by the operation definition.

findings.matchRationaleMd: This finding is operation-specific narrative for the same matched ValueSet-expand operation. It is not a generic REST rule because the R6 terminology-service table names ValueSet-expand and lists operation-specific parameters.

impact.impactRationaleMd: `$expand` is central to terminology service use. If the R6 table is read as mandatory parameter support, R4-compatible terminology servers that lack paging or text-filter support can fail R6 conformance despite the R6 operation page preserving the older statement that servers are not obliged to support paging.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `ValueSet-expand` is standards-status `normative` and FMM 5. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A terminology service migrates from R4 to R6 and advertises terminology capability. It implements `$expand` but not paged expansions; an R6 test suite generated from the terminology-service table treats `offset` and `count` as required support and fails the server.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: R6 could clarify that the table lists parameters a terminology service must recognize only when the corresponding feature is supported, or split baseline `url`/`filter` support from optional paging support with a separate capability signal.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: That would preserve the R4 paging-optional contract but would not establish paging as a uniform baseline for all R6 terminology services if that was the intended goal.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The change may be a reasonable attempt to define a stronger terminology-service baseline, but the local R6 sources are not internally clear because the operation page still says paging is optional. Standards clarification is needed before judging the break proportionate.

evidence.detail: R4 terminology-service narrative summarizes expansion inputs as optional and does not include the reviewed R6 operation support table.
evidence.quote: The client passes the server ... the value set ... optionally a text filter ... optionally which page to retrieve ... optionally other parameters.

evidence.detail: R6 introduces a terminology-service operations table with associated level and required input parameters.
evidence.quote: A FHIR Terminology Service SHALL support the following operations with the associated level and required input parameters.

evidence.detail: The R6 table row for ValueSet-expand lists type and instance support and parameters url, filter, offset, and count.
evidence.quote: ValueSet-expand ... Type Level Yes ... Instance Level Yes ... url ... filter ... offset ... count

evidence.detail: The R6 operation page retains the older paging-optional language.
evidence.quote: Servers are not obliged to support paging, but if they do, SHALL support both the offset and count parameters.

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The runtime endpoint is unchanged, but conformance tooling may use the R6 terminology-service table to require support for parameters that the OperationDefinition still marks optional and that the operation page says may be unsupported. This primarily affects servers, certification tests, and capability claims rather than ordinary R4 client requests.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: If claiming R6 FHIR Terminology Service behavior, document whether `filter`, `offset`, and `count` are supported and test against both the OperationDefinition and the terminology-service table. If paging is not supported, make that limitation explicit in CapabilityStatement or TerminologyCapabilities until the R6 table/prose relationship is clarified.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A stronger baseline for terminology services is a reasonable R6 goal, especially for common UI expansion workflows. The less-breaking design would be to reconcile the table with the operation page by distinguishing required operation support from optional paging support. Without that clarification, R4 servers can face avoidable conformance ambiguity.

findings.title: Terminology-server CapabilityStatement advertisement shifts from system-level to ValueSet resource-level, while base remains system-level

changedFields.note: The R6 terminology-server example advertises the operation where the OperationDefinition says it is valid: on ValueSet type/instance, not as a system operation.
The base CapabilityStatement continues to advertise a system-level `expand` with a lower-case definition URL in both R4 and R6, so local R6 CapabilityStatement signals are not fully aligned.

findings.matchRationaleMd: The CapabilityStatement entries reference the same ValueSet-expand operation being reviewed. The operation itself keeps `system:false`, `type:true`, and `instance:true`, so the advertisement level is operation-specific.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Capability-driven clients that searched only `CapabilityStatement.rest.operation` for a system-level `expand` entry in the R4 terminology-server statement may miss the R6 example's ValueSet resource-level advertisement. Conversely, the unchanged base CapabilityStatement still exposes a system-level signal, which can keep generated conformance tests inconsistent.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `ValueSet-expand` is standards-status `normative` and FMM 5. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A client uses a server's CapabilityStatement to decide whether `$expand` is available. It checks system-level operations because that is where the R4 terminology-server artifact advertised `expand`, but an R6 terminology-server example lists it under the ValueSet resource instead.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: R6 could align all core CapabilityStatements by advertising ValueSet-expand at resource level and, if transitional compatibility was desired, explicitly document any legacy system-level entry as non-authoritative or deprecated.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Advertising both levels would help old capability parsers but would conflict with `system:false` and could imply a `[base]/$expand` operation that the OperationDefinition does not support.

freshReview.rationaleMd: Moving the terminology-server example to resource-level looks correct for the operation, but the remaining base system-level advertisement makes the overall R6 capability signal ambiguous. The practical impact is tooling/conformance rather than direct wire-format failure.

evidence.detail: R4 terminology-server CapabilityStatement advertises expand as a system-level operation.
evidence.quote: level system, mode server, name expand, definition OperationDefinition/ValueSet-expand

evidence.detail: R6 terminology-server example advertises expand under the ValueSet resource.
evidence.quote: level resource, resource ValueSet, mode server, name expand, definition http://hl7.org/fhir/OperationDefinition/ValueSet-expand

evidence.locator: CapabilityStatement-base.json in R4 and R6 packages
evidence.detail: The base CapabilityStatement entry remains system-level and uses lower-case valueset-expand in both versions.
evidence.quote: level system, mode server, name expand, definition http://hl7.org/fhir/OperationDefinition/valueset-expand

evidence.detail: The R6 OperationDefinition itself says the operation is not system-level but is type and instance-level.
evidence.quote: system false; type true; instance true

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: CapabilityStatement-driven discovery can look in different places for the same operation. A client or conformance test generated from the R4 terminology-server statement may expect a system operation; a client generated from the R6 example should look under `rest.resource[type=ValueSet].operation`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When advertising R6 `$expand`, put the operation under the ValueSet resource and include the canonical OperationDefinition URL. For compatibility with older capability parsers, document any legacy system-level advertisement carefully and avoid implying support for `[base]/$expand` unless the server intentionally offers a non-standard extension.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The inferred R6 goal is to align advertisement with the operation's actual invocation levels. That is reasonable, but R6 would be less confusing if all core CapabilityStatements used the same level and casing. Keeping a legacy system-level entry as the only signal would be less breaking for old parsers but would perpetuate a route that conflicts with the OperationDefinition.

findings.title: R6 explicitly treats omitted abstract as allowing abstract codes

changedFields.oldValue: If this parameter has a value of true, the client is stating that the validation is being performed in a context where a concept designated as 'abstract' is appropriate/allowed to be used, and the server should regard abstract codes as valid. If this parameter is false, abstract codes are not considered to be valid.
changedFields.newValue: If this parameter has a value of true or the parameter is omitted, the client is stating that the validation is being performed in a context where a concept designated as 'abstract' is appropriate/allowed to be used, and the server should regard abstract codes as valid. If this parameter is false, abstract codes are not considered to be valid.
changedFields.note: The computable cardinality and type remain `0..1 boolean`; the behavioral change is in the parameter semantics for omission.

parameterDeltas.name: abstract

oldValue.documentation: If this parameter has a value of true, the client is stating that the validation is being performed in a context where a concept designated as 'abstract' is appropriate/allowed to be used, and the server should regard abstract codes as valid. If this parameter is false, abstract codes are not considered to be valid.

newValue.documentation: If this parameter has a value of true or the parameter is omitted, the client is stating that the validation is being performed in a context where a concept designated as 'abstract' is appropriate/allowed to be used, and the server should regard abstract codes as valid. If this parameter is false, abstract codes are not considered to be valid.

parameterDeltas.impactMd: An R4 client that omitted `abstract` because it wanted ordinary validation may receive a successful R6 validation for an abstract grouping code unless it now sends `abstract=false` explicitly.

findings.matchRationaleMd: The R4 and R6 artifacts have the same id, canonical URL, operation code `validate-code`, resource `ValueSet`, and `system=false`, `type=true`, `instance=true` invocation flags. The shard is a direct canonical-url comparison rather than a replacement or rename analysis.

impact.impactRationaleMd: `ValueSet/$validate-code` is a common normative/FMM 5 terminology operation, and accepting abstract grouping codes by default can change validation results rather than only metadata. The risk is occasional because it only manifests when the candidate code is abstract and the caller omits the parameter; however, that is exactly the default shape R4 callers may use. The evidence does not prove that all R4 servers treated omission as false, so this is a potential runtime and conformance change rather than a certain wire break.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: R4 baseline for `ValueSet-validate-code` is standards-status `normative` and FMM 5. For this R4→R6 analysis, that R4 maturity/status is the stability pressure. R6 maturity/status is not used to increase the burden for breaking R4 clients or servers.

findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Clients should set `abstract=false` explicitly whenever validating codes for contexts that require concrete selectable concepts, and should set `abstract=true` when abstract grouping concepts are acceptable. nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 makes the idempotent/no-state-change property computable
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds `affectsState=false`, but both R4 and R6 operation pages already label `$apply` idempotent. This improves machine-readable metadata without changing the intended behavior.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Servers should verify that `$apply` implementations do not persist returned activities as a side effect; persistence should be a separate create/update action chosen by the caller.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds computable type-level scope for the activityDefinition input
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The new R6 `scope` value makes computable the existing prose that `activityDefinition` is required for type-level invocation and not allowed for instance-level invocation. The accepted request shape does not materially change.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated request validators may now enforce the type-only placement directly; legacy tests that sent `activityDefinition` on an instance call should be corrected.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 clarifies that $apply results are transient proposed activities
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The added R6 prose clarifies that no resources created by the operation are persisted and that the returned result represents a proposal. This is consistent with the operation being idempotent in both versions and with the caller deciding how to carry out the proposed activity.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: If an implementation historically persisted resources during `$apply`, treat that as behavior needing redesign for R6 conformance rather than as a new required output shape.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: OperationDefinition.name is normalized while code and canonical URL are unchanged
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 uses `name: Data Requirements`; R6 uses `name: DataRequirements` and `title: Data Requirements`. The executable identity remains the canonical URL and `$data-requirements` code, so clients and servers using the operation route are unaffected.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Catalog or code-generation tooling that used `OperationDefinition.name` as a display label may need to prefer `title` in R6 or key by canonical URL/code. This is metadata/tooling churn, not a runtime operation break.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly declares the operation non-state-changing
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 has no computable `affectsState` value for this operation, but the R4 operation page already says the operation is idempotent. R6 `affectsState: false` formalizes the same behavior and supports safe GET/read-only handling.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tools that surface `affectsState` can treat the R6 declaration as confirmation that existing read-only invocation behavior is still intended.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Status and maturity advance from draft trial-use FMM 2 to active normative FMM 3
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The maturity and standards-status changes increase stability expectations for future changes but do not alter the invocation URL, parameter contract, return type, or operation semantics for R4 clients and servers.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Conformance documentation may describe the operation as more stable in R6. Because no behavior-significant field changed, this does not create an R4-to-R6 migration burden.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds the CanonicalResource $current-canonical operation
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Moved out of material findings during reduction because this item is reverse-only or purely additive R6 behavior. The current report is scoped to R4→R6 compatibility: whether R4 clients, servers, generated code, validators, conformance tests, or existing operation contracts break when moving to R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Treat `$current-canonical` as discoverable optional R6 functionality rather than a baseline assumption when interoperating with mixed-version systems. R6 servers that implement it should advertise the operation where appropriate, enforce the required unversioned `url`, allow repeated `status`, compare candidate versions using `versionAlgorithm`, and return either no `result`, one concrete canonical resource in `Parameters.parameter[name=result]`, or an `OperationOutcome` when currentness cannot be determined.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: OperationDefinition.name is normalized while code and canonical URL are unchanged

nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 has no computable `affectsState` field for this operation, but the R4 operation page already labels it idempotent. R6 `affectsState: false` formalizes a non-state-changing/idempotent signal rather than removing an R4 input or endpoint.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The operation comment in both versions still says submitted data is posted to the receiving system and can be used for later measure calculation. Implementers should verify intended server-side persistence semantics instead of relying on `affectsState: false` alone.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds SHOULD-level guidance for per-subject Bundles, dataUpdateType, and X-Provenance
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The new narrative uses SHOULD-level language and resource/profile guidance; it does not add a new OperationDefinition parameter, binding, invariant, or required output.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Quality-reporting implementations should review `MeasureReport.dataUpdateType`, reporter/provenance expectations, and the Data Exchange for Quality Measures profile guidance when adopting the R6 payload model.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 candidate explicitly declares product $everything non-state-affecting
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 did not have a computable `affectsState` element on this artifact, but the rendered R4 page already stated the operation is idempotent. R6 `affectsState: false` makes that read-only behavior computable.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators and conformance tools can use `affectsState: false` for R6 operation metadata, but existing clients do not need to change request parameters or response handling because of this flag.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 candidate preserves the R4 product $everything Parameters contract
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The candidate keeps `_since`, `_count`, and direct Bundle `return` cardinalities and primitive/resource types unchanged. Implementers must migrate the resource route, but not the operation's input/output Parameters shape.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Existing R4 handler logic for paging and incremental retrieval can usually be reused after remapping resource identity and returned-resource models.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 replaces the R4 MedicinalProduct $everything identity and route with MedicinalProductDefinition $everything
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Moved out of material findings during reduction because this item is reverse-only or purely additive R6 behavior. The current report is scoped to R4→R6 compatibility: whether R4 clients, servers, generated code, validators, conformance tests, or existing operation contracts break when moving to R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Migrate operation registries and generated methods from `MedicinalProduct-everything` to `MedicinalProductDefinition-everything`, and update route tests from `/MedicinalProduct/.../$everything` to `/MedicinalProductDefinition/.../$everything`. Continue sending `_since` as `instant`, `_count` as `integer`, and expecting a direct `Bundle` searchset result.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly declares MedicinalProductDefinition $everything non-state-affecting
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 did not have an `affectsState` element in the computable artifact, but the R4 operation page already described the operation as idempotent. R6 `affectsState: false` is a computable confirmation of the same read-only behavior.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tooling that uses `affectsState` can treat the R6 operation as safe/idempotent without changing the request or response contract.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 changes display metadata while preserving the executable `$everything` code
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 used `name: Fetch Product Record`; R6 uses `name: Everything` and `title: Fetch Product Record`. The executable operation code remains `everything`; clients should not construct the `$everything` route from the human display name.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Metadata catalogs and generated documentation may display a different OperationDefinition name/title, but runtime invocation remains based on `code: everything` and the resource context.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 makes the state-changing classification explicit with affectsState=true
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 omitted `affectsState`, but the R4 rendered operation page already labeled the operation non-idempotent and the narrative already required POST. The required `content` parameter is a complex `Bundle`, so R4's general OperationDefinition method rule did not require GET support even without the explicit flag. R6's `affectsState: true` is therefore a computable clarification of existing operation behavior.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Metadata comparison tools and generated operation registries should expect the R6 artifact to expose statefulness directly. This may change generated labels or safety gates, but it should not require changing the actual `$process-message` request route or body.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 clarifies empty successful responses and fixes asynchronous example typos
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 already documented 204 No Content and asynchronous 200 OK with no body, so R6's `if not empty` qualifier on the Bundle response content-type rule is a consistency clarification. The example query parameter correction from `aync=true` to `async=true` and the callback operation correction from `$process-messages` to `$process-message` match the unchanged operation parameter and code.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Conformance tests should continue to permit documented empty response cases and should use the corrected `async=true` query parameter and `$process-message` callback spelling when updating examples.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 normalizes operation metadata without changing the wire contract
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 changes metadata from R4 `name: Process Message`, `status: draft`, standards-status `trial-use`, and no `title`/`experimental` element to `name: ProcessMessage`, `title: Process Message`, `status: active`, `experimental: false`, standards-status `normative`, and WG `inm`. The canonical URL, id, operation code, route, and parameters are unchanged, so this is metadata/tooling churn rather than runtime behavior change.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated documentation or code that uses `OperationDefinition.name` as a symbol may see the normalized R6 name, but interoperable invocation should continue to use the canonical URL and operation code `process-message`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds an optional date input for historical preferred identifier lookup
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Moved out of material findings during reduction because this item is reverse-only or purely additive R6 behavior. The current report is scoped to R4→R6 compatibility: whether R4 clients, servers, generated code, validators, conformance tests, or existing operation contracts break when moving to R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 servers should implement `date` consistently with the operation prose and include tests for omitted date, current date, historical date, and dates outside any applicable identifier period. Clients that must interoperate with R4 servers should feature-detect R6 support or avoid sending `date` when calling R4 endpoints.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: The required-bound type input can use additional R6 NamingSystem identifier type codes
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Moved out of material findings during reduction because this item is reverse-only or purely additive R6 behavior. The current report is scoped to R4→R6 compatibility: whether R4 clients, servers, generated code, validators, conformance tests, or existing operation contracts break when moving to R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Update R6 server validation and generated client enums for `type` to include `iri-stem` and `v2csmnemonic`. Mixed-version clients should map R6-only type requests to R4 only by explicit policy, such as using `other` for legacy v2 mnemonic lookup if the R4 server documents that behavior.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Operation metadata is normalized and promoted without changing the canonical operation identity
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 changes metadata such as `name` (`Fetch Preferred it` to `PreferredId`), `title` (`Fetch Preferred id`), status (`draft` to `active`), publisher/work group, and standards status (`trial-use` to `normative`). The canonical URL, operation code, resource context, and invocation path are unchanged, so clients route and invoke the same operation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Documentation generators and dashboards may show the new display name and normative status. Code that keys operation behavior by canonical URL or operation code should not need a rename.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds NamingSystem $translate-id as a new type-level idempotent operation
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Moved out of material findings during reduction because this item is reverse-only or purely additive R6 behavior. The current report is scoped to R4→R6 compatibility: whether R4 clients, servers, generated code, validators, conformance tests, or existing operation contracts break when moving to R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Treat `$translate-id` as an R6 feature. R4 clients should continue to use R4-supported routes such as `$preferred-id` where appropriate. R6 clients should feature-detect support through CapabilityStatement and then follow the R6 input contract: required `id`, `sourceType`, and `targetType`, with optional `preferredOnly` and `date`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 $translate-id output Parameters are ambiguous and internally inconsistent
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Moved out of material findings during reduction because this item is reverse-only or purely additive R6 behavior. The current report is scoped to R4→R6 compatibility: whether R4 clients, servers, generated code, validators, conformance tests, or existing operation contracts break when moving to R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Until the ballot issue is resolved, R6 clients should defensively handle both `targetIdentifer.preferred` and `targetIdentifier.preferred`, should not assume a lone top-level preferred or period parameter applies to every returned identifier, and should report ambiguity when multiple target identifiers are returned. R6 servers should include the required `result` boolean if implementing the current OperationDefinition and document any temporary support for the corrected spelling.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 CapabilityStatement advertises $translate-id with a differently cased definition URL
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Moved out of material findings during reduction because this item is reverse-only or purely additive R6 behavior. The current report is scoped to R4→R6 compatibility: whether R4 clients, servers, generated code, validators, conformance tests, or existing operation contracts break when moving to R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 servers and derived CapabilityStatements should advertise the exact OperationDefinition URL casing. Tooling that consumes ballot4 metadata may need a temporary case-insensitive fallback or a known-alias map for this operation, but that should be treated as a workaround rather than the desired base behavior.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds a broader identifier translation operation alongside retained $preferred-id
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The operation is additive relative to R4 and does not remove the existing `$preferred-id` operation from R6. Its broader behavior can return all available target identifiers when `preferredOnly=false`, which is useful but not a direct R4 compatibility break.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementers should not map `$preferred-id` calls blindly to `$translate-id`; `$translate-id` requires both `sourceType` and `targetType` and may return multiple target identifiers plus metadata.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 makes the existing idempotent behavior computable with affectsState=false
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds `affectsState=false`, but R4 already presented the operation as idempotent in the rendered operation page. This is a computability improvement rather than a runtime behavior change.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tools that distinguish an omitted boolean from explicit `false` may see metadata churn, but clients and servers should continue to treat `$lastn` as non-state-changing.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Operation metadata name/status changed without changing canonical URL or code
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 changes `name` from `Last N Observations Query` to `Lastn`, moves the display phrase into `title`, and changes status from draft/trial-use to active/normative. The canonical URL, operation code, invocation endpoint, and CapabilityStatement operation name remain stable.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated documentation or registries that display `OperationDefinition.name` may update labels, but routing and conformance matching should key on canonical URL and operation code.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 clarifies that grouping codes can be discovered rather than explicit in the request
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R4 operation already allowed category parameters and code-bearing search parameters; R6's added note explains a consequence of that existing model rather than adding a new input requirement.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Clients should be aware that `$lastn` groups may include concrete `Observation.code` values that were selected indirectly through category or `code:below` queries.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds optional `include-statuses` input parameter
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The new parameter is optional (`min=0`, `max=*`) and the R6 narrative says that when it is absent the default is to include all statuses except `entered-in-error`, matching the R4 default exclusion. Existing R4 requests remain shape-valid in R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 clients that rely on status filtering, especially including or excluding specific Observation.status values, need to confirm server support before calling R4 or mixed-version servers. R4 downgrade cannot represent this operation option except by omitting it and accepting the default behavior.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Operation metadata was normalized and maturity advanced
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 changes `name` from the R4 display-like `Observation Statistics` to `Stats`, adds title `Observation Statistics`, changes status from draft to active, and explicitly sets `experimental=false`. The canonical URL, id, operation code, and invocation URL remain stable, so the wire behavior is not renamed.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tooling that labels or generates wrappers from `OperationDefinition.name` rather than canonical URL or operation code may see a class/display-name change, but clients should key operation compatibility on canonical URL and `$stats` code.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 rendered pages still document Patient `$everything` with the R4-compatible shape
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Considered by itself, the R6 rendered operation page preserves the R4 canonical URL, Patient type/instance routes, idempotence statement, and parameter table. The break arises because the R6 package and operations registry do not expose the same computable artifact.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Human readers may continue to implement Patient `$everything` from the R6 page, while package-driven tooling may omit it. Migration plans should account for that mismatch.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 operation narrative adds version-specific reference guidance and trims R4 US-Realm wording
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The rendered R6 narrative says servers SHOULD resolve version-specific references by returning the explicitly named version and replaces the R4 US Realm / meaningful-use sentence with a general IG statement. This changes conformance guidance but does not change request parameter names, requiredness, repeatability, or output type in the rendered table.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Servers with Patient `$everything` support should review whether their included resources preserve version-specific references. US Realm minimum-content requirements should be sourced from applicable IGs rather than from the base operation narrative.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 rendered narrative clarifies there is no defined result order
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 already said there was no inherent user-display order and that servers might sort by descending last update. R6 restates this as no defined order and changes the sorting language to MAY, so this is a clarification rather than a new incompatible ordering contract.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Clients should not rely on Bundle entry order for Patient `$everything`; use resource metadata or explicit application sorting if order matters.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 formalizes read-only behavior and normalizes operation metadata
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 changes `status` from draft to active, standards-status from trial-use to normative, `name` from the long display phrase to `Match`, adds `title`, and sets `affectsState: false`. These affect catalogs, maturity review, and generated labels, but the canonical URL, `$match` operation code, Patient type-level invocation, and idempotent behavior are unchanged.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Operation catalogs should key on canonical URL and `code`, not display `name`. Review tooling should use R6 normative/FMM 5 status as stability pressure for semantic changes, not as a standalone runtime break.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 clarifies searchset Bundle output and updates the match-grade extension link
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds explicit return documentation that the Bundle type is `searchset` and changes the narrative link text for `match-grade` from the local R4 extension page to `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/match-grade` hosted in the FHIR extensions package. R4 already required search scores, described empty search sets, and examples used the same canonical match-grade extension URL, so the operation response contract is not materially reshaped.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Clients should continue to expect a direct searchset Bundle of Patient matches, optionally with OperationOutcome information. Compatibility issues inside Bundle entries or the match-grade extension definition should be tracked in the relevant resource/extension review rather than as a Patient $match parameter change.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds non-mandatory guidance about inactive patients and merges
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds narrative text saying implementers should consider the relevance of returning inactive patients, especially around merges, and gives examples where an inactive merged patient may be excluded or otherwise included. The text remains algorithm-specific guidance and does not add a parameter, mandate a fixed return policy, or change the base Bundle output type.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Servers should document inactive-patient and merge handling as part of their MPI behavior. Clients should not infer a portable base guarantee beyond the returned Patient records, search scores, and match-grade extensions.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds the Patient $purge operation
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Moved out of material findings during reduction because this item is reverse-only or purely additive R6 behavior. The current report is scoped to R4→R6 compatibility: whether R4 clients, servers, generated code, validators, conformance tests, or existing operation contracts break when moving to R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Do not assume `$purge` exists on R4 or on every R6 server. R6 clients should check server CapabilityStatement support and should invoke the instance URL only when explicitly supported. Cross-version packages should model `Patient-purge` as an R6-only standard operation or as a custom R4 operation if a deployment backports it.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Patient $purge is marked non-state-changing despite destructive purge semantics
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Moved out of material findings during reduction because this item is reverse-only or purely additive R6 behavior. The current report is scoped to R4→R6 compatibility: whether R4 clients, servers, generated code, validators, conformance tests, or existing operation contracts break when moving to R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Until the R6 metadata is clarified, implementers should treat `Patient-purge` as state-changing despite `affectsState=false`: require POST, enforce authorization and audit controls, and document any idempotent repeat behavior separately from GET safety. Test suites should not require GET support for this operation without explicit standards clarification.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 base CapabilityStatement advertises Patient purge as a system operation with a mismatched canonical URL
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Moved out of material findings during reduction because this item is reverse-only or purely additive R6 behavior. The current report is scoped to R4→R6 compatibility: whether R4 clients, servers, generated code, validators, conformance tests, or existing operation contracts break when moving to R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Do not derive a system-level Patient purge route from the R6 base CapabilityStatement entry alone. Implementers should align advertisements with the exact `OperationDefinition/Patient-purge` canonical and the instance-level route. Validators and conformance tests should flag the case and level mismatch rather than treating the system-level entry as authoritative for Patient-purge.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds optional type-level url/version selectors for the PlanDefinition
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 keeps the existing optional inline `planDefinition` input and adds optional type-scoped `url` and `version` parameters as another way to identify the PlanDefinition. R4 clients that send `planDefinition` still have an R6-compatible request shape for that selector.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 clients that use `url` and `version` cannot send those parameters to a pure R4 server without a compatibility transform; they need to resolve the canonical PlanDefinition and send it as `planDefinition`, or invoke the operation at the instance level when available.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 makes the planDefinition input type-scoped in computable metadata
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 already said in prose that `planDefinition` is required for type-level invocation and not allowed for instance-level invocation. R6's `scope: ["type"]` makes that rule machine-readable.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated validators may now enforce the placement directly; legacy tests that placed `planDefinition` on an instance-level call should be corrected or treated as relying on behavior already disallowed by R4 prose.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 makes the idempotent/no-state-change property computable
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds `affectsState=false` and clarifies that results are transient and not persisted by the server. The primary operation pages for both versions already identify `$apply` as idempotent, so this is a clearer machine-readable contract rather than a new operation side effect.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Servers should verify that `$apply` does not persist generated requests as a side effect. Persistence should be performed by a separate caller action if the proposed activities are accepted.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 normalizes operation metadata and explicitly marks the operation as non-state-changing
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R6 changes are metadata-only for this operation: the computable `name` is made code-safe, `title` is added, status/maturity metadata advances, `experimental: false` is explicit, and `affectsState: false` is explicit. The canonical URL, operation code, invocation flags, parameter list, and narrative behavior remain the same, so R4 clients and servers do not face a different wire contract.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Metadata-driven tools should key operation routing and compatibility on `url` and `code`, not on the display-like `name`. Tools that use `affectsState` can treat the R6 operation as explicitly safe/read-only; R4 metadata consumers had to infer that from the operation description or local policy.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 makes read-only/idempotent behavior computable with `affectsState: false`
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The computable R6 flag matches the R4 rendered page's idempotency statement rather than changing the operation's statefulness.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tooling that previously inferred read-only behavior from the R4 page can read `affectsState: false` directly from the R6 OperationDefinition.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 normalizes display metadata while retaining draft status
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 `name` was `Convert from one form to another`; R6 uses `name: Convert` and `title: Convert from one form to another`. The canonical URL, code, route, and status remain stable, so this is metadata/tooling churn rather than an operation behavior break.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems that display operation names may show a shorter R6 label, but should continue to key behavior on canonical URL and code.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: The separate `$graphql` operation remains available but is not a `$graph` replacement
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is not itself a breaking change for the assigned `$graph` shard; it is noted only to prevent a false rename/replacement conclusion.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: `$graphql` can be a redesign option for some retrieval workflows, but clients must supply GraphQL queries and handle Binary JSON output rather than sending a GraphDefinition URI and receiving a Bundle.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly declares Resource $graphql non-state-affecting
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 does not serialize a computable `affectsState` value in this artifact, but the R4 operation page already states that Resource `$graphql` is an idempotent operation. R6 `affectsState: false` formalizes the same behavior for tools that distinguish read-only operations from state-affecting operations.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated clients, routers, or conformance tests can use R6 `affectsState: false` as confirmation that Resource `$graphql` may use read-only/idempotent handling. This does not require changing an R4-conformant client or server that already followed the R4 operation narrative.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Operation display, status, and standards metadata are normalized without changing the wire contract
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 used `name: Execute a graphql statement`, `status: draft`, standards-status `trial-use`, and FMM 1. R6 uses `name: Graphql`, `title: Execute a graphql statement`, `status: active`, standards-status `normative`, and FMM 1. The canonical URL, operation code, invocation flags, parameters, and response documentation remain stable, so clients and servers using the operation route are unaffected.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Catalogs or generated labels that displayed `OperationDefinition.name` may need to prefer `title` for the long label in R6. Review tooling should treat the standards-status change as stability context, not as a runtime operation break.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds formal system-level invocation and computable `affectsState: false`
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This expands the formal R6 route set rather than removing an R4 route. The R4 Resource operation page already described the operation as idempotent, and R6 makes that computable with `affectsState: false` while adding `[base]/$validate` to the formal URLs.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 clients may use `[base]/$validate` for cross-resource validation, but R4 servers generated strictly from the R4 OperationDefinition may only support type and instance routes even though the R4 base CapabilityStatement advertised `validate` at `rest.operation`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds many optional validator-control input parameters
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The new inputs are all optional and do not alter the required output shape. They standardize options that validators may already expose, including graph validation, usage context, language, jurisdiction, extension handling, QuestionnaireResponse questionnaire handling, warning/severity switches, publication checks, markdown/security controls, verbose output, and example URL handling.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 clients that depend on these switches need R6-aware endpoints and should not assume R4 servers will accept unknown operation parameters. R6 servers should document defaults, because several new parameters explicitly leave defaults to server discretion.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 clarifies that malformed content can make validation fail with 4xx/5xx
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 already said 4xx/5xx means validation itself could not be performed. R6 gives examples such as invalid character set or broken JSON, which reads as clarification rather than a new response contract.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Clients should continue to distinguish a successful validation operation returning an OperationOutcome with errors from an HTTP failure where validation could not be performed.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 makes the type-level scope of `definition` and `url` input parameters computable
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 narrative already said that when the operation is called at instance level, `definition` and `url` are ignored. R6's `scope: ["type"]` on those input parameters makes that existing behavior computable and does not remove a meaningful R4 invocation because the OperationDefinition is not system-level.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated R6 clients may expose `definition` and `url` only on the type-level operation method and omit them from instance-level overloads. Instance-level callers should rely on the instance id in the URL rather than passing these parameters.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 normalizes operation metadata and advances maturity/status without changing protocol identity
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R4 `name` value `Generate Snapshot` changes to R6 `Snapshot`, with the human-readable label preserved as `title: Generate Snapshot`; status changes from draft/trial-use to active/normative. Runtime dispatch depends on operation code `snapshot`, endpoint URLs, and canonical URL, all of which are unchanged.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tools that generated display labels or class names from `OperationDefinition.name` may see source-level churn. Prefer canonical URL, id, and code for stable matching.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds optional inline map inputs to StructureMap $transform
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Moved out of material findings during reduction because this item is reverse-only or purely additive R6 behavior. The current report is scoped to R4→R6 compatibility: whether R4 clients, servers, generated code, validators, conformance tests, or existing operation contracts break when moving to R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: For R4-to-R6 migration, keep existing `source` URI plus `content` request builders working and regenerate operation helpers to expose the optional R6 map-supply inputs. For clients that need one code path against both R4 and R6 servers, prefer the R4-compatible `source` URI form and pre-register required maps on the server, or negotiate/version-check before using `sourceMap`, `supportingMap`, or `srcMap`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Operation display/status metadata is normalized in R6
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 changes metadata such as `name` from `Model Instance Transformation` to `Transform`, adds `title: Model Instance Transformation`, sets `experimental: false`, changes publication status from draft to active, and changes standards-status context to normative. These do not alter the canonical URL, operation code, invocation endpoints, required inputs, or output contract.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tooling that displays operation names should prefer the canonical URL/code for identity and treat the R6 `name`/`title` split as metadata churn rather than a new operation.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 makes read-only behavior computable with affectsState false
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R4 operation page already states that `$transform` is idempotent. R6's `affectsState: false` makes the same behavior explicit for computable clients and CapabilityStatement/OperationDefinition tooling.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Clients and conformance tests can treat the operation as read-only/idempotent in both releases, while using the R6 computable flag when available.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds the Subscription $events operation
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Moved out of material findings during reduction because this item is reverse-only or purely additive R6 behavior. nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Treat `$events` as an optional R6 capability. Discover support through server documentation or CapabilityStatement/operation discovery before calling it, and retain fallback recovery paths such as re-querying affected resources when absent. When implementing the R6 operation, accept inclusive `integer64` bounds, treat `content` as an optional hint, apply documented retention/availability policy, and return a direct `subscription-notification` Bundle with first entry `SubscriptionStatus`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 standardizes an optional missed-event recovery operation
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The operation is new in R6 and optional for servers; no R4 core route or parameter contract was found to be invalidated.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Mixed-version clients should feature-detect support and keep R4-compatible recovery fallbacks. R6 responses depend on R6 subscription notification artifacts, so R4 downgrade paths need a custom/backport policy.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds an idempotent Subscription `$status` operation

nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: No R4 operation migration is required. Servers adopting R6 should implement the operation only where they support topic-based Subscription status reporting and should return a direct searchset Bundle.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 base CapabilityStatement advertises `$status` with system-level placement and a non-matching canonical
