nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Treat the OperationDefinition itself as authoritative for invocation: implement and call `Subscription/$status` or `Subscription/[id]/$status`, not `[base]/$status`. Tooling should canonical-match carefully and tolerate this ballot artifact only as a known issue if necessary. Server-specific R6 CapabilityStatements should publish the exact OperationDefinition URL and place the operation under the Subscription resource operation list when support is offered.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds optional $expand inputs for filtering, supplements, properties, value set version policy, manifests, and transaction-supplied resources
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The added inputs are all optional: `filterProperty` 0..* code, `useSupplement` 0..* canonical, `property` 0..* string, `handle-unclosed-expansion` 0..1 boolean, `default-valueset-version`/`check-valueset-version`/`force-valueset-version` 0..* canonical, `manifest` 0..1 canonical(Library), and `tx-resource` 0..* Resource. Existing R4 request shapes do not need to supply them.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 clients using these parameters need feature negotiation or graceful fallback when calling R4 servers. `handle-unclosed-expansion=false`, value set version policy parameters, and `tx-resource` can intentionally change server behavior, so clients should not assume R4 semantics when they are present.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 makes idempotence computable with affectsState:false
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 operation narrative already said `$expand` is idempotent on the ValueSet operation page. R6 `affectsState:false` makes that expectation computable rather than changing the runtime contract.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generators can use `affectsState:false` to classify the operation as safe from a state-change perspective, while still treating expansion results as transient terminology content as both versions describe.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds optional input controls for terminology validation behavior
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The added inputs are optional: `useSupplement` 0..*, `lenient-display-validation` 0..1, `valueset-membership-only` 0..1, `inferSystem` 0..1, `system-version` 0..*, `check-system-version` 0..*, `default-valueset-version` 0..*, `check-valueset-version` 0..*, `force-valueset-version` 0..*, `manifest` 0..1 canonical(Library), and `tx-resource` 0..* Resource. R4 request shapes remain valid, but R6 clients have more standard controls for display strictness, system inference, version policy, manifests, supplements, and caller-supplied terminology artifacts.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R4 servers or bridge layers may reject these new parameters if R6 clients send them. Upgraded servers should either implement the requested behavior or return clear operation errors rather than silently ignoring controls such as version overrides or `lenient-display-validation` that can affect validation results.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 widens displayLanguage from one code to many
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 allowed `displayLanguage` `0..1`; R6 allows `0..*` and states that the display value only needs to match one requested language. This is a widening for R4 callers because a single language remains valid.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6-to-R4 downgrade of a request with multiple `displayLanguage` parameters is lossy unless a bridge chooses one language or fans out multiple R4 calls. Conformance tests should distinguish this reverse-direction limitation from an R4-to-R6 break.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 makes type-level scope computable for selected value-set selector inputs
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds `scope: ["type"]` for `url`, `valueSet`, and `valueSetVersion`. This is consistent with the narrative distinction that non-instance calls need a way to identify the value set, while instance calls already identify the ValueSet in the URL.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated R6 validators may enforce the scope column. If an R4 client sent `url`, `valueSet`, or `valueSetVersion` on `[base]/ValueSet/[id]/$validate-code`, move that selector to `[base]/ValueSet/$validate-code` or omit it when the instance URL already identifies the value set.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 makes the idempotent/no-state-change property computable
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R6 `affectsState=false` field matches the idempotence statement already present on both R4 and R6 operation pages. It improves machine-readable metadata without changing the intended runtime behavior.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Servers should continue treating validation as a read-only terminology operation. Capability and security tooling can now use the computable R6 flag instead of relying only on page prose.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 normalizes display metadata without changing the wire operation
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 used `name: "Value Set based Validation"`; R6 uses machine-friendly `name: "ValidateCode"` and `title: "Value Set based Validation"`. The canonical URL and operation code remain unchanged, so clients invoking `$validate-code` are not affected.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Catalogs or documentation generators should key operation identity by canonical URL or `code`, not by the human-facing `name` field.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds a draft Patient named-query OperationDefinition example
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Moved out of material findings during reduction because this item is reverse-only or purely additive R6 behavior. The current report is scoped to R4→R6 compatibility: whether R4 clients, servers, generated code, validators, conformance tests, or existing operation contracts break when moving to R6.
